papers.title: Predicted state-to-state collisional rate coefficients from neural networks
papers.summary: Molecular spectra observed in the interstellar medium are commonly analyzed using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium models, which requires accurate state-to-state collisional rate coefficients. Close-coupling calculations become prohibitively expensive for transitions from highly excited rotational states, therefore available datasets are often truncated at low initial states and temperatures; and since each new system also requires an accurate ab initio potential energy surface, many detected molecules have no collisional data. We employ two machine learning strategies to predict rotational state-to-state rate coefficients of molecules included in the train set beyond the range of initial states and temperatures computed so far, and predicting those of a molecule absent from training and validation sets. Feed-forward neural networks are trained on state-to-state de-excitation rate coefficients of 24 linear molecules colliding with para-H2. Scheme 1 includes all systems in the train+validation set, with 70%, 80%, and 90% initial-state boundaries and a 90% temperature boundary. Scheme 2 is trained on 22 systems described only by transition and molecular properties, and predicts two excluded systems, CS and CF+, whose astrophysical impact is explored with non-LTE calculations. For the 90% boundary, Scheme 1 predicts 99.4% of the test transitions within a factor of 2, and no prediction deviates from the reference value by more than a factor of 4.7. This model was used to complete 18 datasets. Scheme 2 reproduces the rate coefficients of two excluded systems within a factor of 3 for more than 92% of their transitions. Both schemes provide near-instantaneous complements to close-coupling calculations: Scheme 1 extends the range of a molecule already included in the training set with high accuracy, while Scheme 2 gives a reasonable first estimate for a molecule that has not been studied.

papers.title: Riemannian Hessian analysis of Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem
papers.summary: Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem are Riemannian gradient descent methods on the sphere under a metric induced by a discrete elliptic operator. We analyze their convergence through the condition number of the Riemannian Hessian at the ground state. Bounds of the Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian give a uniform analysis of these methods for different metrics. The uniform analysis applies to the classical metrics, such as the shifted Laplacian and the energy-adaptive metrics. Inspired by this analysis, we also consider three new metrics. One of them is a Thomas--Fermi metric, whose condition number is bounded uniformly in the interaction strength for the one-dimensional harmonic trap and whose iteration count does not grow in the Thomas--Fermi regime in the numerical tests. The performance suggested by our analysis is consistent with three-dimensional numerical tests with up to one billion unknowns, for both Riemannian gradient descent and Riemannian conjugate gradient methods, whose practical performance is also related to the Hessian condition number. The Thomas--Fermi flow needs the fewest iterations, while the metrics inverted exactly by tensor-product solvers are the fastest in computational time on one GPU card.

papers.title: Quantum Information-Theoretic Analysis of Optical Fiber Sensing via Stimulated Brillouin Scattering
papers.summary: Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is a powerful mechanism for distributed sensing in optical fibers, as the Brillouin response is highly sensitive to local material parameters. Assuming the input probe is a quantum state, we develop a quantum-information-theoretic framework for SBS-based fiber sensing and intrusion detection. Starting from a linearized opto-acoustic Hamiltonian, we derive an effective input-output relation for a short fiber segment. We then model each fiber segment as a single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel and the entire fiber as a cascade of quantum channels. We then compute the quantum Fisher information for general SBS-dependent parameters and identify optimal measurement settings to achieve the quantum limit, comparing them with receiver-constrained strategies such as heterodyne detection and photon counting. In addition, we propose an adaptive approach that achieves first-order asymptotic optimality and provides a novel second-order correction to address preliminary miscalibration. As an application, we apply the framework to the fiber-tapping detection problem.

papers.title: All-optical deconvolution via quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy with bright twin beams
papers.summary: The resolution of spectroscopic measurements is fundamentally limited by the convolution between a system's intrinsic response and the instrument response function, creating an ill-posed inverse problem. While entangled photons can theoretically bypass these limits, low photon flux has hindered their experimental realization. Here, we propose quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy (QCCS), utilizing macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler beams) to physically circumvent this convolution limit in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering. Employing the signal beam as a broadband probe, QCCS achieves all-optical deconvolution through a correlation-enhanced sum-frequency generation channel between the convoluted anti-Stokes and idler beams. By subtracting the uncorrelated background using a 500-femtosecond temporal window, we successfully retrieve narrow Raman bands (8 cm^{-1} and 15 cm^{-1}) completely obscured by a 75 cm^{-1} probe bandwidth without numerical deconvolution or prior knowledge. Our results establish macroscopic quantum correlations as a robust resource for high-fidelity spectroscopy, paving the way for ultrashort-pulse-free operando studies under natural, incoherent excitation conditions.

papers.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
papers.summary: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential field-induced phase transition into a collective electronic state driven by enhanced electron-electron interactions. Our findings provide valuable insights into the unconventional chiral transport and emergent correlated quantum states under extreme magnetic fields.

papers.title: Ultrafast laser-stimulated field emission from a metal: a non-equilibrium Green's functions approach
papers.summary: Ultrafast laser-assisted field emission from metallic nanotips is a promising route for generating coherent electron pulses. However, existing theoretical models often neglect many-body strong correlation effects in the emitter's electronic structure and its response to the optical field. In this work, we propose a theoretical framework based on the non-equilibrium Green's function formalism to simulate the out-of-equilibrium electron dynamics across a strongly driven matter-vacuum interface, in a one-dimensional model. Treating the tip-vacuum coupling perturbatively, we find that the interplay between strong-field emission and multi-photon emission regimes can be described in terms of a filtering of the emitter's local density of occupied states through field-dressed vacuum propagators. By including electron-electron interactions via the second-Born approximation, we show that correlation-induced modifications in the electronic structure are directly transferred to the far-field spectrum. Finally, by self-consistently solving the Dyson equation at the interface, we uncover a dynamic back-action regime driven by the optical field, characterized by a periodic polarization of the emitter, which reshapes the far-field spectrum. This shows that the non-equilibrium Green's functions approach provides a versatile framework for exploring and analyzing field emission of correlated electrons.

papers.title: Solitons in the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with the pseudo-Raman term, anti-diffusion gain and nonlinear loss
papers.summary: We introduce a nonconservative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLSE) which includes additional nonlinear terms accounting for the pseudo-stimulated-Raman-scattering (pseudo-SRS) effect and cubic loss. An essentially novel feature of the model is the linear anti-diffusion gain, which leads to the obvious blow-up in the infinite or spatially periodic system. We consider the absorptive boundary conditions, which suppress the blow-up driven by effective convective instability in the setup. The NSLE model is derived, in the extended adiabatic approximation, from the underlying Zakharov system, which includes the viscosity term acting on its low-frequency component and the anti-diffusion gain in the high-frequency (HF) one. The latter term appears if the expansion, with respect to the deviation of the wavenumber, is performed not around the minimum-loss point (as in the usual situation), but around a maximum-loss point. Dynamics of moving solitons in the model is addressed by means of analytical and numerical methods. The sech approximation for the soliton predicts it as a stable fixed point (FP) of the system of balance equations for the HF norm and wave momentum, derived in the moving reference frame. The FP attraction basin is identified too. The predictions are corroborated by direct simulations of the full NSLE with the absorptive boundary conditions.

papers.title: Resistive alignment of a black-hole magnetosphere
papers.summary: Recent numerical simulations have shown that black-hole magnetospheres evolve rapidly toward alignment between the magnetic axis and spin axis but the physical origin of this process has remained unclear. We develop an analytic theory of this alignment within resistive relativistic magnetohydrodynamics. Taking the slow-spin Blandford-Znajek monopole solution as the exterior magnetic field, we reduce the induction equation to a relaxation equation for the current-sheet inclination angle. Our analysis shows that alignment results from second-order spin effects in the Blandford-Znajek solution combined with explicit resistive dissipation. We test this prediction using resistive-GRMHD simulations at several spins and resistivities and find a regime in which the measured late-time secular decay agrees quantitatively with the analytic prediction.

papers.title: Global Optimization of Beam Profiles for Suppressing the Bump-On-Tail Instability
papers.summary: A particle beam with constant intensity that propagates into a plasma triggers a bump-on-tail instability. It has been demonstrated that beam modulation can be used to significantly reduce this instability. However, finding the optimal beam profiles that accomplish this is a complex optimization problem that suffers from an extremely rugged optimization landscape and a relatively high-dimensional parameter space. In this paper, we evaluate a number of optimization algorithms and find that population based methods (in particular, CMA-ES and Differential Evolution) perform best. In particular, we investigate beam profiles where the beam is either completely turned ON or OFF. This configuration is easier to accomplish experimentally, but leads to a higher-dimensional and thus more challenging optimization problem. We obtain ON/OFF beam profiles that reduce the instability by more than 80% and thus perform significantly better than what has been reported in the literature.

papers.title: Quantitative Eshelby stability: local and finite-shape theory through AI-assisted mechanics
papers.summary: How can human researchers use artificial intelligence (AI) to make progress on difficult mechanics problems while retaining control of physical significance, mathematical rigor, and validation? We explore this opportunity through a quantitative stability problem rooted in the Eshelby conjecture. For a uniform dilatational eigenstrain in a homogeneous isotropic solid, we establish a nonlinear two-sided relation between whole-interior strain heterogeneity and a geometry-only distance from the ellipsoid family, with half-order Sobolev scaling that captures morphological length scale. We then develop a complementary finite-shape theory: ellipsoidal subtraction yields an exact residual-field budget from which systematically convergent upper and lower bounds are obtained for a prescribed geometry. Applied to protruded, indented, and necked inclusions, the bounds agree with independent displacement-based finite-element calculations. The study also documents a human-led, AI-assisted research process in which researchers select consequential problems, shape targets, audit arguments, require independent checks, and interpret mechanics, while AI broadens analytical exploration and supports computation. This experience also led us to develop Open Problems in Mechanics, a versioned community-facing map that makes selected mechanics questions, their known/open boundaries, and criteria for progress explicit.

papers.title: VN-GraphGG: von Neumann--Mullins--based graph grain growth simulation
papers.summary: Efficient simulations of grain growth are essential for investigating the process-structure-property relationships in polycrystalline materials. We introduce a two-dimensional von Neumann-Mullins-based graph grain growth simulation (VN-GraphGG), which couples the grain-scale kinetics with microstructure reconstruction. The polycrystalline microstructure is represented as a graph with grain and junction nodes. The grain-area evolution on the grain graph is governed by the von Neumann--Mullins (VN) law, while a graph neural network is trained to reconstruct the microstructure from the graph. This separation allows kinetic coefficients to be varied without retraining the neural reconstruction model. Topological changes during grain growth such as disappearance of grains and changes in neighbor relations are handled straightforwardly through reconstruction and postprocessing. Simulations demonstrate accurate predictions of VN kinetics and coarsening statistics, and significant speedup over the phase-field simulations. The proposed method provides a foundation for efficient grain growth simulation based on grain-scale kinetics, opening the way to incorporate a broader range of physical mechanisms. An application example is presented for abnormal grain growth, in which kinetic heterogeneity significantly influences the grain microstructure evolution.

papers.title: Predicting Nanofabrication Variance: A Conditional Diffusion Model
papers.summary: Micro- and nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam (FIB) milling invariably deviate from input designs due to systematic and stochastic effects such as ablation-rate fluctuations, and redeposition. As such, nominally identical iterations of a given process yield a distribution of non-identical fabrication outcomes, leading to variations in the physical (optical, mechanical) properties of fabricated structures. Existing models of the milling process typically predict a single deterministic fabrication result, neglecting this variability. Here we present a conditional diffusion model that learns the statistical distribution of process outcomes conditioned on input design, enabling it to predict a realistic distribution of possible output sample structures. These predictions accurately reproduce edge morphology, linewidth variations, and defect probabilities observed in fabricated samples, enabling statistical analysis of milling performance and the identification of dominant structural and process parameter-dependent deformation modes. The work establishes a probabilistic modelling framework for fabrication variability analysis and fabrication-aware design optimization.

papers.title: A new device for live cell imaging of biological samples under in-plane shear
papers.summary: The effect of mechanical stresses and deformations upon the behavior and properties of cells and tissues is a topic of paramount interest in the field of biophysics. Its understanding is essential for deepening our comprehension of cellular responses to environmental stimuli, with implications in fields ranging from embryogenesis to tumor development. For boosting the understanding in this field, it is important to develop devices for the application of simple deformations in order to probe the cellular response to the basic mechanical transformations. While a number of stretching devices have been developed, in-plane shearing deformation has been little investigated. Here, a new device is introduced that allows the application of homogeneous in-plane shear upon a cell monolayer while imaging the sample with a commercial optical microscope. A description of the faced experimental challenges is reported and a full characterization is presented. It is demonstrated the capability of the device to apply reproducible, controlled and homogeneous shear of both single cells and confluent cellular monolayers.

papers.title: The Hydrological Cycle and Circulation of Tidally-Locked Planets with a Finite Moisture Inventory
papers.summary: Tidally-locked planets express a range of climate regimes distinct from those found in our solar system. Their atmospheres are often dominated by planetary-wide overturning circulations and super- rotating jets. In this paper we explore the hydrological cycle of such planets and how it might depend on the total inventory of condensate. To this end we use a set of idealised GCM simulations to probe the response of the hydrological cycle to the surface moisture budget in their atmospheres. We find that for low moisture inventories the climate quickly develops a barren day side and a moist night side where the moisture is trapped, as might be expected. For higher moisture inventories the drying of the day side is significantly delayed by the development of a substellar lake just east of the substellar point, which is sustained by the presence of a local thunderstorm-like convective system that persists even after the lake disappears. The timescales for the lake to disappear are millennia, suggesting that even a weak transfer of moisture through surface processes could maintain a moist day side. We also find that adjusting the threshold at which the evaporative rate becomes constrained by the remaining surface liquid depth modifies the longevity of the lake and surrounding day side conditions. These findings have implications for understanding a diverse range of planetary climates and habitability, given the distribution of moisture and presence of a substellar lake.

papers.title: Latin squares as a model of perfect mixing of high-entropy alloys
papers.summary: The structure of high-entropy alloys, which include 5 or more components in equimolar proportions, is proposed to be described in the mathematical language of Latin squares. This model is fundamentally discrete and allows for a quantitative description of ideal mixing, in which any given alloy element is guaranteed not to have an identical element as its nearest neighbor. For the two-dimensional case, the model possesses four axes of translational symmetry, which makes it possible to tile the plane with a single Latin square and, based on the properties of this square, describe the properties of macroscopic material samples. The model makes it possible to make quantitative estimates of the suitability of a particular atomic structure (configuration) for implementation in a perfectly mixed high-entropy alloy with maximum mixing entropy. A condition has been obtained for acceptable fluctuations in the concentration of components at which the thermodynamic stability of the alloy is maintained. The possibility of identifying superstructures in high-entropy alloys based on group theory, as applied to the description and construction of Latin squares, is discussed. Based on the proposed model, the probability of forming a multicomponent alloy with ideal mixing is estimated. For a five-component alloy, this probability is no more than 2.6*10^{-10}.

papers.title: First Experimental Results of Space Object Detection Using the InteRFeX Array
papers.summary: This paper presents the first experimental validation of InteRFeX, a non-uniform receive only (passive) array located at the Nova Systems Space Precinct in Peterborough, Australia, designed for space domain awareness applications. It operates over a frequency range of 70 to 300 MHz and is capable of functioning in a range of observational modes, including as a coherent passive bistatic radar for space surveillance, which is the focus of this work. InteRFeX exploits commercial broadcast transmissions as illuminators of opportunity, combining cross-ambiguity function processing for bistatic range and range-rate retrieval with MUSIC-based direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for angular localization. The International Space Station (ISS) serves as the experimental target, with measurements evaluated against Two-Line Element (TLE) orbit predictions. Taking advantage of the dual-polarized array, all four reference--surveillance polarization combinations are evaluated, revealing differences in detection rate and mean signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) over the observation pass, with bistatic-range RMSEs of approximately 1 km relative to the TLE-derived reference. Independently, the MUSIC-based DoA estimates exhibit a mean angular separation of approximately $0.45^\circ$ from the TLE-derived reference directions. The angular deviations are further decomposed into along-track and cross-track components, enabling a more detailed characterization of the DoA offsets relative to the TLE-derived reference trajectory. The processing framework also includes a first-order bistatic link-budget analysis to estimate the expected SNR over the observation geometry. These results demonstrate the feasibility of passive-radar space domain awareness using radio-interferometric array technology and establish the proposed signal-processing pipeline as a basis for a dedicated coherent passive-radar mode within InteRFeX.

papers.title: Warning of infrastructure deformation anomaly through probabilistic analysis of InSAR observations
papers.summary: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) offers a low-cost, wide-area solution for near continuous infrastructure monitoring. However, translating InSAR observations into automated anomaly warnings remains challenging because displacements are relative, affected by uncertainty, and acquired along line of sight (LOS). We introduced a probabilistic warning framework that accounts for these factors. LOS displacements were modelled through a Gaussian distribution. A limit state function was defined to describe the displacement exceedance, and the time-dependent probability of exceedance was evaluated. Instead of a fixed threshold, warnings were identified through abrupt increases in exceedance probability. The framework was validated using three case studies of quay walls in Amsterdam, providing timely anomaly warnings and issued no warnings for the non-collapse case. Results demonstrate the potential of a probabilistic interpretation of InSAR time series for deformation anomaly warning.

papers.title: Magnetic connectivity from the Sun to the Earth with MHD models II. Impact of input magnetic maps
papers.summary: Connectivity estimation needs to be fast and thus usually relies on semi-empirical models. We previously established that optimised magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) models can also be used to derive magnetic connectivity, yielding good results, especially for complex configurations. However, the modelling is not the only factor that can impact the connectivity estimation. Models' results, both semi-empirical and MHD, depend heavily on the input data used to drive the simulation. In order to quantify this impact on our connectivity estimation, we used 20 different maps by four providers. We selected the period of July 2019, which corresponds to Carrington rotation (CR) number 2219, because it had already been studied in a previous paper. It corresponds to a period of minimum activity, meaning minimal interference from transient structures, but with a high-speed stream and several polarity switches. We have compared our results with in situ data from ACE and developed several visualisation techniques to validate connectivity not only for a specific date but also for a full CR. The choice of the input magnetic map drastically affects the connectivity estimates, with global scores going from 28% global agreement to 63% in the most extreme case. The HMI and GONG maps consistently gave the best connectivity estimations, with more than 50% correct results of the full CR. For this specific period, the GONG-ADAPT maps yielded the least reliable results, with a score below 35%. This is not surprising, as we have shown before that COCONUT required parameter adjustments for these maps. However, WSO maps which showed poor coronal agreement actually provided good connectivity estimates, showing that the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS) location is in the end the most crucial parameter for connectivity. Consistent data over a full Carrington rotation are to be favored compared to daily.

papers.title: Encoding Matters: A Qubit-Efficient Reformulation for Quantum Resilient Routing
papers.summary: Qubits are powerful computational resources because each additional qubit doubles the size of the accessible state space. This expressive power comes at a cost: adding qubits also increases circuit size, constraint overhead, and exposure to hardware noise. These limitations are especially critical for near-term quantum computers, making the number of qubits required to formulate a problem a central practical concern. In this work, we present a method for efficiently mapping logistics and routing problems onto qubits through structure-aware encoding reduction. We demonstrate the method on a benchmark problem of latency-resilient routing under dual-link failures. For this benchmark, the reduced formulation substantially lowers both the qubit count and the compiled circuit complexity while preserving the original optimization task. By running the reduced model on the same trapped-ion quantum computer as the benchmark, we obtain a 100X improvement in the success probability. This finding shows how careful problem formulation can make current quantum hardware substantially more effective for practical optimization.

papers.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
papers.summary: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{-1}$. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high $p_\mathrm{T}$. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

papers.title: Judd-Ofelt analysis and coherent spectroscopy of europium-based molecular complexes for quantum information applications
papers.summary: Rare-earth-ion based molecular crystals are emerging as a promising platform for quantum information applications, combining long optical coherence times with the chemical tunability of coordination chemistry. Here we present a comprehensive optical characterisation of twelve Eu$^{3+}$-based molecular complexes, with a focus on the coherent $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition at $\sim$580 nm. Judd-Ofelt analyses are performed across all complexes, providing insights into ligand-field environments, local point-group symmetries, and the resulting branching ratios of the coherent transition. We find that lower point-group symmetry (C$_1$, C$_2$) yields higher branching ratios of the $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition, exceeding 1\% in several complexes. Optical inhomogeneous linewidths measured at 4.2 K reveal narrow linewidths for some complexes of below ten GHz, indicative of a highly ordered crystalline environment. Optical coherence measurements of one of the complexes, 5-Eu, yields an optical coherence time of $T_{\text{2}}^{\text{opt}} = 2.3~\mu\mathrm{s}$ at 4.2 K, comparable to the best-performing molecular systems reported to date. Systematic characterisation and quantitative comparison will be key to find structure-property relations guiding rational design of optimised complexes for quantum information applications.

papers.title: Shear-driven arrest of dip-coating film entrainment
papers.summary: A plate withdrawn from a bath of partially wetting liquid entrains a film above a critical velocity. Here, we show that this critical threshold can be substantially increased by the presence of a laminar gas flow opposed to the plate velocity that exerts a tangential shear stress on the liquid-gas interface. Using two-phase immiscible Navier-Stokes simulations and confining the gas to a narrow channel, we derive a closed-form expression for the interfacial stress, which combined with lubrication theory relates the thickness of the film and the contact line velocity to the applied shear stress. As the gas velocity is increased, the film thins and the contact line velocity slows down, until the imposed shear overcomes the drag of the moving plate and entrainment is arrested. As in the quiescent case, the velocity mismatch between plate and contact line is independent of the plate velocity and is set by the applied shear alone. We find that one set of varying gas flow simulations, with constant critical plate velocity, therefore determines the critical gas flow for every smaller plate velocity.

papers.title: Warm-IP: A Path-Following ADMM Warm Start for Interior-Point Quadratic Programming
papers.summary: Interior-point (IP) methods are powerful second-order optimization algorithms but can make slow progress during early iterations. We propose Warm-IP, a hybrid framework that combines a path-following variant of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with a primal--dual IP method. The ADMM phase generates a warm start that remains close to the central path, enabling the subsequent IP phase to rapidly refine the solution to high accuracy. We evaluate Warm-IP on a diverse collection of real-world and synthetic quadratic programming (QP) instances and compare it with leading commercial solvers (MOSEK and Gurobi) and open-source solvers (Clarabel, PIQP, and OSQP). We also curate and release a new benchmark of large-scale QPs from cancer radiotherapy treatment planning, built from real patient data and provided in canonical QP form, with instances containing hundreds of thousands of constraints. Warm-IP substantially outperforms existing solvers on large-scale problems. On the large-scale radiotherapy benchmark comprising 60 lung cancer cases, for example, Warm-IP solves an instance in 47 seconds on average with no failures, while the strongest competitors, MOSEK and Gurobi, average 55 seconds with failures on 23\% of the cases and roughly 240 seconds with no failures, respectively. To support reproducibility and future benchmarking, we publicly release the implementation and benchmark data through a \href{https://github.com/Radiotherapy-Optimization/Warm-IP}{GitHub repository}. These results demonstrate that appropriately warm-started IP methods can combine the rapid initial progress of first-order methods with the high-accuracy convergence of second-order methods.

papers.title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
papers.summary: Experiments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions determine centrality from final-state quantities, usually the charged-particle multiplicity. Performing the same in hydrodynamic simulations requires millions of events, which is impractical for state-of-the-art hybrid models, and centrality is therefore commonly approximated by the initial entropy or energy. We show that neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict the event-by-event multiplicity and mean transverse momentum $[p_T]$ with relative errors of 1--2\%, which makes it possible to generate millions of collisions at a small fraction of the cost of the full simulation. For Pb--Pb collisions at $2.76$~TeV and Au--Au collisions at $200$~GeV, the initial-state and final-state definitions select nearly the same events in 10\%-wide classes, but up to 20\% of the events change class when the classes are 1\% wide. We then compute the fluctuations of $[p_T]$ and its Pearson correlations with a proxy of the elliptic flow, estimated from the initial eccentricity, and with multiplicity. The first correlation is insensitive to how centrality is defined, while the second changes substantially. The approach can be applied at every design point of Bayesian analyses at modest additional cost.

papers.title: Precision Tokenization for Multi-Modal Data in High Energy Physics
papers.summary: Foundation models have recently gained significant attention in fields such as high energy physics (HEP). The tokenizers that convert detector data into discrete inputs for such models, however, are comparatively unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by learning discrete and compressed tokenized representations of HEP datasets. We demonstrate the approach on four modalities covering two different simulated detectors that vary in complexity. Treating tokenization as a rate-distortion problem, a systematic hyperparameter scan yields four design rules for tokenizing HEP data that hold across all set-based modalities studied. The cost of tokenization is evaluated on tasks including jet $p_T$ regression, particle flow reconstruction, and flavor tagging. We find that tokenization preserves much of the information needed for these tasks at compression factors of approximately 4-11$\times$ while keeping the jet $p_T$ resolution below 1%. We also present heptokens, an open-source library for tokenizing HEP data.

papers.title: Unifying spherical convolutions through lifting
papers.summary: We develop a unified description of convolution on the sphere by lifting to the rotation group. A number of definitions of spherical convolution have been proposed, differing in whether the kernel is axisymmetric or directional, whether the output is on the sphere or the rotation group, whether the signals carry spin, and in their computational cost. No unified treatment exists. Regarding the sphere as the homogeneous space $S^2 \cong \text{SO(3)}/\text{SO(2)}$, we lift a spin $s$ field to the rotation group, convolve on $\text{SO(3)}$, and project back to the sphere through the adjoint of the lift for a potentially different spin $s'$. We recover every rotation-equivariant convolution considered previously through constraints on the kernel, spin choices and inclusion or omission of the lift and projection. For maps between fields of fixed input and output spin, we prove that directional kernels, output on the sphere and equivariance cannot be achieved simultaneously. We make explicit that spin fields are sections of associated line bundles, linking the physics and bundle literatures, and express the spin rotation phase as the character of the twist of the section. We present harmonic-space algorithms for the exact and efficient computation of lifted spherical convolutions of band-limited fields by appealing to sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group. All operators are implemented in the open-source s2conv code, and numerical experiments confirm the reductions and the equivariance of the operators to machine precision. Finally, we illustrate the operators on fields measured on the Earth and on the celestial sky.

papers.title: An Omni-Temporal Framework for Hydrodynamic Dispersion and Reaction in Porous Media
papers.summary: Many applications involve porous-media transport driven on time scales comparable to the pore-scale diffusion time, for which classical pseudo-steady dispersion models based on time-invariant transport coefficients may become inaccurate. While frequency-dependent dispersion has been studied in non-reactive porous media, a corresponding framework that simultaneously accounts for advection, diffusion, and heterogeneous interfacial reaction remains lacking. We address this gap by introducing an omni-temporal framework based on volume averaging of the frequency-domain pore-scale advection-diffusion equation subject to a Robin boundary condition spanning the full range of interfacial reactivity. The resulting upscaled formulation yields four frequency-dependent transfer functions: a dispersion tensor, an advection-suppression vector, a spectral Sherwood number, and a reactivity-bias vector, with the reactivity-bias vector introduced here for the first time. Analytical solutions for fully developed flow between parallel plates and through circular tubes reveal distinct kinetics- and diffusion-limited regimes, including capacitive and semi-infinite Warburg-type frequency responses. Comparisons of transient breakthrough curves with direct numerical simulations demonstrate substantial improvement over conventional pseudo-steady dispersion, particularly for short-duration pulses. Application to a periodic array of square rods under cross flow further demonstrates the frameworks applicability beyond canonical geometries.

papers.title: Demonstration of on-chip all-optical switching of magnetization in integrated photonics
papers.summary: Ultrafast all-optical magnetization switching (AOS) holds great promise for nextgeneration spintronic memory and hybrid spintronic-photonic systems. However, most implementations to date rely on bulky free-space optical setups, limiting scalability and practical integration. As a critical step toward integrated applications, we demonstrate single-pulse AOS within a silicon nitride (Si3N4) photonic integrated circuit. Using trains of femtosecond laser pulses guided through on-chip waveguides, we achieve deterministic toggle switching in a sub-micron out-of-plane Co/Gd Hall cross patterned directly atop the photonic waveguide. Electrical readout via the anomalous Hall effect reveals a switching contrast of up to 90% for 500 nm-wide devices. In larger Hall crosses, the contrast decreases and switching becomes stochastic, consistent with spatially non-uniform optical absorption as confirmed by finite-element simulations. This behavior is hypothetically attributed to domain wall relaxation and thermally assisted (de)pinning processes within partially switched regions. Our results highlight the critical role of device scaling in achieving robust on-chip AOS and establish a foundation for ultrafast, energy-efficient, and fully integrated spintronic-photonic platforms.

papers.title: Dynamic mixed turbulence modeling using a super-resolution generative adversarial approach
papers.summary: A dynamic mixed super-resolution model (DMSRM) for large-eddy simulations (LESs) is proposed, which combines the traditional dynamic mixed model (DMM) formulation with the generation of super-resolved velocity fields from which the subfilter-scale (SFS) stress tensor can be computed. A data-driven super-resolution generative adversarial network (SR-GAN) is employed to upsample the grid-filtered velocity fields by a factor of two, enabling the evaluation of both scale-similarity and the dynamic Smagorinsky contributions. A priori analyses of forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence (HIT) show that the SR-GAN accurately reconstructs flow features and generalizes well across different filter sizes and higher Reynolds numbers within the same flow configuration, even for unseen input fields. The DMSRM reproduces SFS stresses and energy dissipation more accurately than the traditional DMM. A posteriori LES calculations further confirm that DMSRM predicts the energy spectrum and intermittency more accurately than DMM, even for different LES grid-scale resolutions and higher Reynolds numbers than those used for training within the same forced HIT flow configuration. Unlike DMM, DMSRM yields realistic backscatter and physically consistent SFS energy dissipation. These improvements arise from the physically accurate super-resolved fields generated by the SR-GAN, from which SFS stresses are directly computed. The result is a closure that accurately reproduces stress magnitudes and dissipation while reducing reliance on additional dissipation from the dynamic term. The DMSRM formulation achieves a balance of physical fidelity, robustness, and computational efficiency, offering a promising alternative to traditional DMMs for turbulence LES modeling.

papers.title: The throttling refrigeration system for high cooling power recovery of the PandaX-xT cryogenic distillation system for radon removal
papers.summary: The PandaX-xT cryogenic distillation system for removing radon (Rn) is designed to operate at a high liquid flow rate of 856 kg/h, equal to 5 liters per minute (LPM), to meet the required Rn concentration. However, it is challenging to maintain a continuous supply of cooling power (20 kW) for the Rn-removal system. This work proposes a throttling refrigeration system to address the power supply problem for the next-generation PandaX-xT dark matter detection experiment. The system utilizes carbon tetrafluoride (R14) refrigerant to recover power based on heat pump principles. The cooling power from the liquid xenon (LXe) in the reboiler at 178 K is transferred to liquefy the gaseous xenon (GXe) in the cryostat through the phase change circulation of R14, enabling xenon (Xe) to return to the detector in the same state as when it was extracted. Consequently, a stable circulation for liquid distillation is established. Given the high cost of Xe, a research and development (R&D) experiment has been conducted to validate the feasibility of this high-cooling-recovery system by using ethanol as a substitute for Xe. Experimental results indicate that the proposed system could achieve a cooling power recovery of 25 kW, with a recovery efficiency of 99%+-0.5%. Additionally, process simulation and optimization of the throttling refrigeration cycle are performed using Aspen Hysys. The deviation between the simulation and experimental results is found to be <3.64%. These findings demonstrate that implementing Rn-removal distillation at a high flow rate is feasible, eliminating the need for liquid nitrogen or cryocoolers. This system could save approximately 3650 m3 of liquid nitrogen per year or reduce power consumption by 230 kW.

papers.title: Determinism and Indeterminism as Model Artefacts: Toward a Model-Invariant Ontology of Physics
papers.summary: This paper argues that, where deterministic and indeterministic formulations agree on empirically corroborated structure while differing in their completion of structure that remains empirically underdetermined, features invariant across these formulations warrant ontological commitment, whereas any warrant attaching to features that vary across them is categorically more provisional. Because deterministic and indeterministic completions are always formally available, while additional grounds for preferring particular completions are contingent and defeasible, empirically corroborated structure alone cannot determine whether reality is fundamentally deterministic or indeterministic, or whether that very distinction belongs only to specific representations of it. On this basis, I advance a model-invariance criterion according to which structural features are candidates for realist commitment insofar as they are empirically corroborated within a regime and preserved across the admissible formulations of that structure. I show how such invariant content can be characterised in mathematically intelligible ways, yielding a fallibilist form of structural realism grounded in model-invariance rather than in the specific form of any given mathematical representation. Features such as conservation relations, invariant measures, symmetries, and probability or correlation structures over observable histories may satisfy this criterion. By contrast, the localisation of modal selection---whether in fine-grained initial conditions, stochastic outcomes, or state-update and collapse mechanisms---may vary across empirically admissible formulations and therefore constitute a gauge-like representational freedom. This framework offers a realist ontology for modern physics that combines empirical openness with resistance to metaphysical overreach.

papers.title: Coupling with opinion dynamics promotes prosocial behavior in multilayer networks
papers.summary: Various theoretical and empirical studies have accounted for why humans cooperate in competitive environments. Although prior work has revealed that network structure and multiplex interactions can promote cooperation, most theory assumes that individuals play dilemma games in all social contexts. However, real-world agents may participate in a diversity of interactions, not all of which present dilemmas. We develop an evolutionary game model on multilayer networks in which one layer supports the prisoner's dilemma game, while the other follows constant-selection dynamics, representing biased but non-dilemmatic competition, akin to opinion or fad spreading. Our theoretical analysis reveals that coupling a social dilemma layer to a non-dilemmatic constant-selection layer robustly enhances cooperation in many cases, across different multilayer networks, updating rules, and payoff schemes. These findings suggest that embedding individuals within diverse networked settings---even those unrelated to direct social dilemmas---can be a principled approach to engineering cooperation in socio-ecological and organizational systems.

papers.title: Exact analytical PGSE signal for diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface using a spectral Laplacian formalism
papers.summary: Objective. To derive an exact analytical expression for the diffusion MRI signal arising from diffusion confined to a cylindrical surface under finite rectangular pulsed-gradient spin-echo (PGSE) gradients, and to develop computationally efficient strategies for repeated model evaluations. Approach. The Bloch-Torrey equation was solved using a spectral matrix formalism of the Laplace operator in the eigenbasis of the cylindrical surface. The resulting signal is expressed as a product of non-commuting matrix exponentials and is valid for arbitrary rectangular gradient durations and separations, without approximations to the diffusion propagator or spin phase distribution. A reduced real spectral basis was introduced to decrease the dimensionality of the problem. Accelerated implementations based on Strang splitting and Gauss-Legendre quadrature were developed for repeated signal evaluations and computation of the spherical mean. The analytical signal was validated against Monte Carlo diffusion simulations. Main results. The exact formulation showed excellent agreement with Monte Carlo simulations over a wide range of cylinder radii and acquisition parameters. The spectral expansion converged rapidly with mode order, and the reduced basis substantially decreased computational cost without loss of accuracy. The accelerated implementations provided large additional speed-ups while retaining controllable errors relative to the exact solution. Significance. The proposed framework extends exact finite-pulse solutions of the Bloch-Torrey equation to diffusion confined to cylindrical surfaces and provides practical implementations for directional and orientationally averaged diffusion MRI signals. It therefore offers an approximation-free reference for assessing faster signal approximations and for applications requiring large numbers of model evaluations.

papers.title: Assessing the Performance of CC2 for Excited-State Dynamics: A Benchmark Study with Pyrazine
papers.summary: During the ultrafast electronic relaxation of pyrazine, the bright state undergoes rapid decay accompanied by coupled electronic and nuclear motion. We investigate the vibrational modes associated with this process using trajectory surface hopping simulations. To enable accurate \emph{ab initio} excited-state dynamics, we apply CC2 analytical gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors within the Q-Chem package. Using both a reduced vibronic coupling model and full-dimensional simulations, we demonstrate that CC2 predicts that the dark $A_\text{1u}$ state actively participates in the initial relaxation and the subsequent dynamics. The full-dimensional simulations yield a $B_\text{2u}$ decay time of 25--26 fs, in good agreement with the experimental measurement of $22\pm3$ fs. Furthermore, we identify the $Q_\text{8a}$ and $Q_\text{9a}$ modes as dominant tuning coordinates whose motions are phase-locked to the population oscillations between the $A_{1u}$ and $B_{3u}$ states.

papers.title: Data-driven oscillator model for turbulent flows with multiple dominant frequencies
papers.summary: The complex dynamics of high-dimensional oscillatory flows can be simplified using phase-reduction analysis, providing a deeper understanding of the flow response to external perturbations. Although phase-based modeling and analysis have been utilized in recent studies on oscillatory fluid flows, their usage is often limited to single-frequency flows due to difficulties in addressing chaotic characteristics, emerging from multiple dominant frequencies with broadband spectra in turbulent flows. In order to overcome this limitation, we propose a data-driven framework that models the dynamics of turbulent flows with multiple dominant frequencies based on a set of oscillators. The representative oscillators are extracted from the flow field data by training specially designed autoencoders. The oscillator dynamics are modeled through a machine-learning technique using neural networks to accurately predict the multi-frequency oscillatory behavior of turbulent flows. We verify the oscillator-based model of the oscillatory turbulent flows by applying the proposed data-driven method to the three-dimensional supersonic turbulent flow over a cavity. We show that the oscillators extracted from the spanwise-averaged pressure field represent the dominant large-scale flow features and reflect the physical characteristics of the turbulent cavity flow. The data-driven oscillator dynamics model with observation-based correction accurately forecasts the oscillatory behavior of the turbulent cavity flow for a long period. The proposed data-driven method for reduced-order modeling of turbulent flows with oscillators will enable deeper investigations of perturbation dynamics and control of turbulent flows.

papers.title: Thin-film nanostructuring of NbTi superconducting resonators for enhanced temperature sensitivity in cryogenic thermometry
papers.summary: The rising complexity of cutting-edge cryogenic systems is currently imposing challenging technical constraints to the monitoring of ultra-cold temperatures through standard commercially available sensors. Among different technologies, superconducting microwave resonators have been recently investigated as ideal candidates for performing on-chip cryogenic thermometry, in reason of their intrinsically low power dissipation, large temperature sensitivities and excellent sub-$\mu$K resolution below 10 K. Through this study, we aim at demonstrating the possibility to enhance the temperature performance of superconducting microwave resonators by means of surface nanostructuring. Different arrays of nanotrenches are strategically patterned on the inductive line of a 1.3 GHz planar resonator, by partially etching a Nb$_{50}$Ti$_{50}$ thin-film, in order to tune the critical transition of the material and, therefore, increase the curvature of the $f_{res}(T)$ response. Although the presence of such thinned superconducting regions introduces larger microwave losses, a 1.5 K decrease of $T_\text{C}$ is recorded, which directly translates into an enhancement of the temperature sensitivity by a factor 10, with respect to a non-nanostructured sensor. A maximum value of $df_{res}/dT = 62 \ \text{MHz/K}$, at 4.2 K, is achieved for the device showing the largest nanotrench width of about 350 nm. These results demonstrate that such a surface nanostructuring approach can be exploited as an effective design strategy to tune the $f_{res}(T)$ response of superconducting microwave resonators. Although this technique is found to introduce additional RF losses into the superconducting device, thereby limiting the achievable temperature resolution to the few-$\mu\text{K/Hz}^{1/2}$ range, we believe that similar approaches could be further investigated for the development of future cryogenic sensors.

papers.title: Dynamics of fast magnetosonic wave turbulence
papers.summary: Fast magnetosonic waves are among the fundamental oscillation modes of astrophysical plasmas. To study their dynamics, we carry out numerical simulations of the wave turbulence kinetic equation, which describes the evolution of the energy spectrum of a set of weakly nonlinear fast magnetosonic waves. This kinetic equation, which involves three-wave interactions, has recently been derived from compressible magnetohydrodynamics in the low-$\beta$ limit (Galtier 2023). It has an exact stationary solution, the Kolmogorov-Zakharov spectrum, corresponding to a direct energy cascade. Here we perform free decay simulations of the kinetic equation for which we propose a Kolmogorov-type phenomenology to explain the temporal decay laws of energy and integral length scale. In the forced simulations, we show that the cascade is in fact composed of a mixture of a forward cascade for counter-propagating waves, and a backward cascade for co-propagating waves, with the former being stronger than the latter. The Kolmogorov-Zakharov energy spectrum in $k^{-3/2}$ is found in the radial direction with an anisotropy due to the amplitude that depends on the angle relative to the strong mean magnetic field. We give the analytical expression of the Kolmogorov-Zakharov constant, which is numerically verified in the high Reynolds number limit. Our study provides a theoretical explanation for certain observations in the solar wind plasma (Zhao et al. 2022), where a regime of weak turbulence has been identified for fast magnetosonic waves, alongside a critical balance regime for strong Alfv\'en wave turbulence.

papers.title: Bayesian Sampling of Structural Ensembles: The Role of Ensemble-Counting Measures
papers.summary: Structural ensemble refinement is widely used to integrate molecular simulations with experimental measurements. While most applications focus on the maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) ensemble, Bayesian sampling of the posterior distribution can provide uncertainty estimates and posterior averages for arbitrary observables. A notable step in this direction was introduced by the Bayesian Energy Landscape Tilting (BELT) framework, where sampling is performed on a family of maximum-entropy ensembles parametrized by Lagrange multipliers. Here, we show that Bayesian sampling in this setting requires an explicit choice of ensemble-counting measure. In particular, the flat measure in Lagrange-multiplier space used in the original BELT formulation leads to a posterior distribution that is formally non-normalizable for finite reference trajectories. We propose the Jeffreys measure as an invariant ensemble-counting prescription, restoring normalizability in the finite-sample situations considered here, and providing a consistent definition of posterior averages. Using both an analytically tractable Gaussian model and maximum-entropy refinement of RNA oligomer simulations, we compare different ensemble-counting measures and show that they can significantly affect Bayesian estimates. The resulting methodology has been implemented in the \texttt{MDRefine} software package.

papers.title: Detector Performance and Dark Matter Sensitivity of CYGNO with HFO-1234ze Gas Admixtures
papers.summary: The CYGNO project develops optical time projection chambers for directional dark matter searches, using a He:CF4 (60:40) gas mixture at atmospheric pressure and a triple-GEM amplification stage. We investigate the addition of 1-10% HFO-1234ze as a hydrogen-containing additive with low global warming potential. The charge response and scintillation light yield are studied with the MANGO prototype, complemented by secondary-scintillation spectroscopy of the baseline mixture and mixtures containing 1% and 2.5% HFO. Increasing the HFO concentration shifts the charge-response curves towards higher GEM voltages and strongly suppresses the scintillation emission in both the ultraviolet and visible bands. We use the measured optical response to estimate the impact on projected spin-independent WIMP-nucleon and spin-dependent WIMP-proton exclusion limits for a CYGNO-like directional detector. Under the assumed detector-response model, the higher optical energy threshold largely outweighs the benefit of the additional light target, although a 1% HFO admixture retains a limited advantage for low-mass spin-dependent interactions. An idealized fixed-threshold benchmark is also considered to illustrate the potential of the modified target composition without the optical threshold penalty.

papers.title: On the ideal magnetohydrodynamic stability of the sheared-flow Z pinch
papers.summary: Sheared-flow Z-pinch stability has previously been studied within ideal MHD primarily through growth rate calculations, which find that even trans-Alfv\'enic sheared flows apparently fail to suppress the kink instability. Here, trans-Alfv\'enic sheared flow is shown to stabilize the MHD kink but also to excite shear-driven instabilities characteristic of high-Reynolds-number supersonic flow. This distinction is evident from the dispersion relations underlying the growth rates, computed as the analytic dispersion function in the complex-frequency plane. Regularization splits this function into adiabatic and resonant parts describing how discrete modes emerge from and interact with the continuous spectrum. The Doppler-shifted flow continuum is then seen to interact with the interchange and kink instabilities in distinct ways. For interchange, the continuum overlaps the instability branch at all wavenumbers, so even sub-Alfv\'enic sheared flow stabilizes profiles modestly beyond the interchange threshold. The kink, by contrast, is shielded from the continuum by a frequency gap, and trans-Alfv\'enic flow is required to Doppler-shift the continuum into resonance with it, giving a geometric picture of the stabilization threshold. But shear-driven instabilities arise at this same threshold, including reflection modes and an acoustic kink. It is these shear-driven modes, not the original MHD instabilities, that dominate the ideal-MHD spectrum in trans-Alfv\'enic conditions. The ideal analysis thus describes the stabilization mechanism while showing that the stability of the sheared-flow Z pinch ultimately rests on non-ideal physics, such as finite orbit width and dissipation.

papers.title: Bounds on Propagation Constants in Dielectric Gratings
papers.summary: We establish analytical bounds on the normalized longitudinal propagation constants $\beta=k_z/k_0$ of modes in lossless dielectric diffraction gratings. If $\epsilon_{\max}$ denotes the maximum relative permittivity, we show that regular modes ($\beta^2\in\mathbb{R}$) satisfy $\beta^2\le\epsilon_{\max}$ despite the lack of a scalar dispersion relation. We further show that the so-called ghost modes ($\beta^2\notin\mathbb{R}$), admitted by the non-Hermitian nature of the associated eigenproblem, satisfy $|\mathrm{Re}(\beta)|\le\sqrt{\epsilon_{\max}}/2$. Both bounds are obtained directly from the Fourier-series formulation of the fully coupled vectorial eigenproblem.

papers.title: CDW-EIS calculations of atomic ionization by bare ions and antiprotons
papers.summary: We present \textit{ab initio} calculations of atomic ionization by bare ions and antiprotons within the continuum distorted-wave eikonal initial-state (CDW-EIS) model. The dataset covers atomic targets from H to Kr, impacted by bare ions over a broad range of projectile charges and by antiprotons. Particular attention is given to elements in periods 3 and 4 of the periodic table, which are relevant to pigment analysis and technologically important materials. The resulting subshell-resolved total ionization cross sections are made openly available through an online repository covering a broad range of projectile--target systems, occupied initial subshells, and projectile velocities. We analyze systematic trends in the cross sections, including their dependence on projectile charge and velocity, binding-energy scaling, and charge-sign effects in proton and antiproton impact. To extend the practical coverage of the database, we also develop a neural-network surrogate, CDWEIS-NN, trained on the subset of the database with projectile charge $|Z_\mathrm{P}|\leq 8$. The network interpolates the CDW-EIS results to additional projectile--target systems and impact energies, reproducing both held-out CDW-EIS calculations and the experimental benchmarks considered in this work with satisfactory accuracy.

papers.title: Towards Accurate MHz Core Loss Measurements

However, large variations in these data shed light on fundamental barriers to accurate MHz core loss measurement. This paper identifies these barriers and presents methods for overcoming them.

papers.title: Bogoliubov-de Gennes spectrum, Cherenkov radiation and recoil of solitons with third-order dispersion underlying optical analogue horizons
papers.summary: Third-order dispersion turns the soliton of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, which underlies optical analogues of event horizons in fibers, into a weakly radiating solitary wave. We compute three of its properties without assuming a thermal emission law. First, the linearized (Bogoliubov-de Gennes) problem must be posed about the stationary state of the dispersive equation: linearizing about the integrable profile produces a complex quartet that is converged in grid and box, grows as the square root of the dispersion strength and is spurious. About the stationary state, on a periodic grid, the zero-mode sector consists of two Jordan blocks of size two and the spectrum is real at the operating point, including negative-energy box modes of the resonant branch. Second, we measure the steady Cherenkov emission of adiabatically prepared solitons from the flux of the radiation behind them, over eight decades. The radiation is phase-matched in the frame of the drifting soliton, and the first-order rate falls short of the measured one by factors of 29 to 45. Expressed through a scaled dispersion coefficient of the local soliton, the measured rate describes launched solitons of three amplitudes; with norm and momentum balance, and no further fitted parameter, it reproduces their recoil and the slow decay of their loss rate; at weak dispersion the loss of a launched soliton is the shedding of its launch mismatch. Third, a census of the asymptotic channels shows that long-wavelength upstream emission requires the chemical potential of the soliton, lowered by the comoving-frame Doppler shift of a drifting soliton, to lie inside the analysis band, which bounds the soliton amplitude. In a kinematic model of the flow the surface gravity has a closed form; the thermal relation and the entanglement built on it are imposed inputs of that model. The construction applies to Raman-free Kerr media.

papers.title: Systemic risk in interbank networks: disentangling balance sheets and network effects
papers.summary: We study how the level of systemic risk empirically observed in an interbank network differs from the expected risk implied by the balance sheets composition of the participating banks, abstracting from the specific configuration of bilateral exposures. To this end, using different contagion models (i.e., interbank asset valuation functions), we measure observed systemic risk on e-MID network data from 2005 to 2012 and compare it with the expected risk generated by a null model: an ensemble of interbank networks whose links represent possible market clearing configurations. This counterfactual is obtained through a maximum-entropy approach that preserves banks' balance sheet variables and diversification patterns, while randomizing the configuration of exposures. We find that the aggregate levels of observed and expected systemic risks are generally consistent but diverge significantly during turbulent periods - specifically following the default of Lehman Brothers (2009) and the VLTRO implementation by the ECB (2012). At the individual level, however, banks often appear more or less risky than implied by their balance sheet alone, due to their position in the network. Our results show, on the one hand, that balance sheet information embedded in a suitable maximum-entropy framework provides reliable estimates of aggregate systemic risk; on the other hand, they highlight the importance of detailed network information for accurate stress testing of individual banks, particularly after systemic events.

papers.title: Superconducting-antiqubit simulation enables optimal phase estimation via unitary inversion
papers.summary: A positron is equivalent to an electron traveling backward through time. Casting transmon superconducting qubits as akin to electrons, we simulate a positron with a transmon subject to particular resonant and off-resonant drives. We call positron-like transmons "antiqubits." An antiqubit's effective gyromagnetic ratio equals the negative of a qubit's. This fact enables us to time-invert a unitary implemented on a transmon by its environment. We apply this platform-specific unitary inversion, with qubit--antiqubit entanglement, to achieve a quantum advantage in phase estimation: consider measuring the strength of a field that points in an unknown direction. An entangled qubit--antiqubit sensor offers the greatest possible sensitivity (amount of Fisher information), per qubit, per application of the field. We prove this result theoretically and observe it experimentally. This work shows how antimatter, whether real or simulated, can enable platform-specific unitary inversion and benefit quantum information processing.

papers.title: Stringent constraints on nonstandard neutrino interactions using high-purity $\nu_{\mu}$ CC events in IceCube DeepCore
papers.summary: The neutral-current (NC) nonstandard interactions (NSIs) of neutrinos with fermions can modify the flavor oscillations of atmospheric neutrinos as they propagate through the Earth. We present constraints on the NC-NSI parameters $\varepsilon_{\mu\tau}$ and $\varepsilon_{\tau\tau}-\varepsilon_{\mu\mu}$ (one at a time) using a high-purity sample of $\nu_{\mu}$ charged-current atmospheric neutrino events collected by IceCube DeepCore over 7.5 years of livetime. These two parameters significantly affect the $\nu_\mu$ disappearance channel for which this golden event sample is optimized by IceCube Collaboration. The best fit to this dataset is consistent with no NSI hypothesis, and we place the stringent constraints $-\,0.0094 < \varepsilon_{\mu\tau} < 0.0079$ and $-\,0.031 < \varepsilon_{\tau\tau}-\varepsilon_{\mu\mu} < 0.029$ at the 90% confidence level, assuming normal mass ordering.

papers.title: Enhancing Event Reconstruction in Hyper-Kamiokande with Machine Learning: A ResNet Implementation
papers.summary: The forthcoming Hyper-Kamiokande experiment is expected to achieve unprecedented sensitivity to neutrino oscillations. Meeting these precision goals requires substantially larger Monte Carlo datasets than previous experiments to satisfy stringent systematic-uncertainty requirements. While traditional maximum-likelihood reconstruction provides high-quality event reconstruction, its per-event computational cost makes reconstruction of large, systematically varied Monte Carlo samples increasingly impractical. We demonstrate a neural-network-based reconstruction approach for the Hyper-Kamiokande far detector using simulated data with the experiment's detector geometry. Single-particle events are generated with kinetic energies from the Cherenkov threshold up to 2 GeV above threshold. The resulting PMT charge and timing information are mapped to $274\times144$ five-channel images that serve as inputs to ResNet models in the WatChMaL framework. These models (i) classify events into four particle hypotheses ($e$, $\mu$, $\gamma$, $\pi^{0}$) and (ii) regress the interaction vertex, direction, and momentum of electrons and muons. The regression models achieve momentum resolutions of $1.27\%$ for muons and $2.21\%$ for electrons, angular resolutions of $0.91^\circ$ and $1.60^\circ$, and vertex resolutions of $13.6\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $17.0\,\mathrm{cm}$, better than those reported for traditional methods. The classifier improves $e$-$\mu$, $e$-$\gamma$, and $e$-$\pi^{0}$ separation relative to the traditional baseline, with ROC AUC values of $0.9999995$, $0.642$, and $0.9659$. Our networks achieve inference times of 1-2 ms per event on a single GPU, yielding speed-ups of $3.2\times10^{4}$-$5.2\times10^{4}$ relative to likelihood-based reconstruction.

papers.title: Mesoscopic theory of flocking with alignment and antialignment copying
papers.summary: We study a stochastic model of collective motion in which individuals update their orientation through pairwise aligning or anti-aligning copying interactions. We analyze both annealed dynamics, where interaction types are chosen probabilistically at each update, and quenched dynamics, where individuals are permanently assigned to aligning or anti-aligning subpopulations. Starting from the microscopic master equation on the circle, we derive an exact mesoscopic description via a Fourier-mode expansion and a systematic large $N$ expansion, obtaining closed Fokker-Planck equations and effective stochastic differential equations for the polarization. We show that competing alignment and anti-alignment suppress long-range polar order in the thermodynamic limit in both cases, while finite systems display nontrivial fluctuation-induced structure controlled by the interaction composition. Our results, validated by Gillespie simulations, establish an analytically tractable framework for collective dynamics characterized by competing copying rules and intrinsic noise.

papers.title: An asymptotic-preserving reduced-order method for parametrised rarefied gas flow by proper generalised decomposition
papers.summary: Modelling rarefied gas flow using the Boltzmann equation is vital in many areas. Because of the high dimensionality and coexistence of multiple characteristic scales, conventional solution strategies for this equation incur prohibitively high computational costs and are inadequate for rapid response in engineering design simulations. Based on proper generalised decomposition (PGD), we propose an a priori, asymptotic-preserving reduced-order method for the high-dimensional parameterised Shakhov kinetic model equation. Separated representations reduce the kinetic problem to a set of low-dimensional problems. We incorporate synthetic equations into the PGD iteration so that, in the hydrodynamic limit, the iteration reduces to solving the Navier-Stokes equations, whose solution naturally exhibits a low-rank structure. Furthermore, treating the rarefaction parameter as an additional coordinate yields a solution over the whole range of rarefaction in one offline computation. It enables fast online queries to any point in the parameter space. Numerical examples using this method show reasonable precision and a significant reduction in computational cost.

papers.title: Certified Bounds on the Measurement Cost of Molecular Hamiltonians
papers.summary: Quantum estimates of molecular energy require repeated state preparation and measurement. We bound the minimum repetition count for given measurements and processing rules from above with a practical schedule and from below with independently verified inequalities. For an H$_4$ chain at H-H distances of 0.90 and 1.80 \AA with 2 per cent uniform noise in the ground state, entangling Clifford measurements, which map Pauli products onto one another, cut leading-order repetitions by at least 65.9 and 61.0 per cent, respectively, relative to any schedule using only single-qubit Pauli measurements and Hamiltonian terms. With 69 unaltered measurement settings, each a basis change followed by qubit readout, processing further observables saves at least 12.04 and 6.70 per cent. For four lanthanide and actinide Hamiltonians with depolarized Hartree-Fock covariances, reducing the sum of absolute Hamiltonian coefficients does not proportionally reduce sampling. The bounds cover linear unbiased estimates from independent batches at small error.

papers.title: Beyond Orbital Rotations: Correlation-Rank Limits and Clifford-Accessible Measurement, from Algebra and Global Optimization
papers.summary: One should not assume that reconstructing an electronic observable with a smaller set of measurement settings will cut the number of repetitions in proportion. Each setting is simply a basis change and qubit readout, but the savings are not guaranteed to be commensurate. Take two electrons of opposite spin in two spatial orbitals: the orbital degree of freedom of each electron acts as a logical qubit and rotations are independent in the spin sectors. From the observable's one- and two-qubit coefficients we derive an exact floor for the setting count and a decomposition to meet it in no more than three settings. With fewer settings, the minimum error in the two-qubit correlation coefficients is set by the singular values left out. A case in point is an exchange with equal nonzero couplings on the three Pauli axes. This demands three orbital settings yet only one joint measurement. We offer a Clifford circuit for four physical qubits to effect the necessary mapping of Pauli products under conjugation. In the case of a one-parameter family of logical singlet-triplet mixtures, the orbital-to-Clifford shot cost ratio is three at maximum mixing and trends toward 3/2 near the logical singlet. Where spin sectors may be mixed, isotropic exchange needs one orbital setting. For spin-conserving Hamiltonians with $N$ spatial orbitals encoded via Jordan-Wigner, the $X$-rank, the binary rank of the $X$ parts of its strings, of any commuting Pauli string family is no more than $2(N-1)$. Searches with the Robust Adaptive Nature-inspired Global Explorer (RANGE) reach this limit for CH$_4$, with the rank of the Hamiltonian support vouching for the maximality of the search values. And for all nonidentity Pauli strings on $n$ qubits, semidefinite witnesses from the Lov\'asz theta number give a lower bound on the Clifford setting count that agrees with the integer cover and counting bounds at $2^n+1$.

papers.title: Optimal Calibration-Free Observable for the Nucleon-Coupling Ratio in a Dual-Alkali Comagnetometer for Dark Matter Searches
papers.summary: A dual-alkali single-cell $^{87}$Rb-$^{39}$K-$^{3}$He comagnetometer can read an axion-like dark matter signal through two optical rotation channels, encoding the ratio $\mathcal{R}=\xi_n/\xi_p$ of the field's neutron and proton spin couplings in their relative response. The inter-species phase difference $\Delta\varphi$ has been proposed as a calibration-free readout that is sensitive to $\mathcal{R}$. Treating the extraction of $\mathcal{R}$ as a statistical estimation problem, we show that the estimate of $\mathcal{R}$ depends on the two channels only through their complex ratio, which splits into $\Delta\varphi$ and an amplitude ratio, of which only $\Delta\varphi$ is insensitive to the relative gain and hence calibration free. For our choice of comagnetometer parameters, above $\sim\!100$ Hz the phase difference alone captures most of the coupling-ratio information. At lower frequencies $\Delta\varphi$ is no longer near-sufficient. Below $\sim\!40$ Hz, the amplitude ratio would improve the precision on $\mathcal{R}$ by a factor of $\gtrsim2$. Recovering that information, however, requires the relative gain to be known sufficiently accurately, so $\Delta\varphi$ remains the robust observable even where it is not the most informative one.
