papers.title: Lee--Yang Zeros and Pseudocritical Drift in J-Q N\'eel Antiferromagnet--Valence-Bond Solid Transitions
papers.summary: Square-lattice J-Q models provide a sign-problem-free setting for probing the quantum phase transition between N\'eel antiferromagnet and columnar valence-bond solid. We analyze this transition through the scaling of Lee--Yang zeros, computed within stochastic series expansion quantum Monte Carlo by reweighting configurations sampled near criticality in the presence of complex source fields. Benchmark studies of the dimerized Heisenberg model and the checkerboard J-Q model validate the method, yielding stable \(\mathrm{O}(3)\) critical scaling in the former and clear spacetime-volume scaling in the latter, as expected for a first-order transition. Applying the same analysis to the J-Q models, we find a pronounced and systematic drift of the leading-zero scaling with increasing system size, consistent with an extended pseudocritical regime. The Lee--Yang scaling implies an effective scaling dimension \(\Delta_{\phi}\) of the \(\mathrm{SO}(5)\) order-parameter field that decreases with size and is consistent with vanishing in the thermodynamic limit. Such behavior lies below the scalar unitarity bound of any unitary relativistic conformal field theory in \(2{+}1\) dimensions and enforces inverse spacetime-volume scaling of the zeros, the hallmark of a first-order transition. These results support a weakly first-order interpretation of the N\'eel--VBS transition and establish the finite-size Lee--Yang zeros as a sensitive, symmetry-resolved diagnostic of pseudocriticality and transition order in the J-Q family.

papers.title: Topologically quantized macroscopic attractor states in hydrated DNA
papers.summary: Driven dissipative systems at ambient conditions typically exhibit continuous responses shaped by fluctuations and relaxation, with discrete macroscopic states arising only under specific dynamical constraints. Here, we report the emergence of discrete attractor states in a quasi-two-dimensional hydrated DNA sample under magnetic excitation. The transverse polarization voltage $V_{xy}$ displays telegraph switching between well-defined levels, indicating stochastic transitions between metastable macroscopic states. Statistical analysis of the voltage time series reveals bimodal distributions and strong Bayesian model selection in favor of multiple coexisting states. A phenomenological phase-field framework describes the observed metastability and switching in terms of a proposed collective $U(1)$ polarization phase. Within this interpretation, phase-slip dynamics and integer-labeled winding sectors provide a possible organizing principle for the discrete macroscopic response. The results suggest that macroscopic quantization can emerge in a classical system at ambient conditions as a consequence of dissipative dynamics constrained by phase topology.

papers.title: Complex surface patterning in homo- and heteroepitaxial contexts: (simultaneous) step bunching and step meandering
papers.summary: We confront a meso-scale continuum model, archetypical for the heteroepitaxial context, with an atomistic Vicinal Cellular Automaton (VicCA), built as a homoepitaxial counterpart, to show that in (2+1)D complex surface instabilities are fundamental growth phenomena rather than context-specific artifacts. Our approach is to first construct a Ginzburg-Landau-type model, designed to extend the previously (1+1)D Tersoff-type models to (2+1)D. We complement the continuum approach with a discrete one - the VicCA, in which we use a novel version of the potential landscape for the diffusing particles - a double-well potential located at each step edge. Importantly, this framework also captures both step bunching and step meandering. While these behaviors are rarely treated together in earlier approaches, they naturally coexist in real materials. Thus we establish a cross-context correspondence at the level of obtained morphologies and morphology diagrams and, additionally, a multiscale perspective on the governing parameters, bridging the gap between the mesoscale and atomistic modeling.

papers.title: Engineering superconductivity on the surface of Weyl semimetals
papers.summary: Ten years after the experimental discovery of Weyl semimetals, theoretical and experimental work has pointed to the possibility of realizing surface-only superconductivity at relatively high temperatures in these materials. A consensus is developing that this unusual form of superconductivity is supported by surface electronic states unique to Weyl semimetals, known as Fermi arcs. In this work, we show that the topological protection of these exotic states can be exploited to engineer high critical temperatures. Motivated by reports of van Hove singularities on the surface of PtBi$_2$-the first Weyl semimetal in which surface superconductivity was unequivocally linked to its Fermi arcs-we demonstrate how such singularities can be engineered through the deposition of a suitable additional layer. We find that the critical temperature becomes extremely sensitive to the exact value of the chemical potential, and values as large as 20 times the bulk $T_c$ can be achieved. More generally, our results demonstrate how topological protection can be exploited to manipulate surface electronic states, thereby opening experimentally accessible routes toward engineering high-temperature two-dimensional superconductivity and other exotic phases.

papers.title: Floquet-Multiple Andreev Reflections
papers.summary: Floquet theory describes quantum systems governed by time-periodic Hamiltonians, much as Bloch theory describes spatially periodic solids. In voltage-biased multiterminal Josephson junctions, the Josephson relation causes superconducting phase differences to evolve periodically in time, thereby providing an intrinsic Floquet drive. In this Letter, we consider three-terminal Josephson junctions formed on a ballistic two-dimensional normal conductor with a continuum of electronic states. We show that the quartet and higher-order multipair processes yield characteristic Floquet-multiple Andreev reflection (Floquet-MAR) finite-bias conductance and noise resonances that are parameterized by the bias voltage and electrochemical potential. This microscopic picture opens a route toward implementing and probing Floquet-MAR physics in ballistic multiterminal Josephson junctions.

papers.title: Spin-orbital exchange as a route to intertwined dipole-quadrupole orbital order in MnV$_2$O$_4$ under strong trigonal crystal field
papers.summary: Orbitally degenerate systems provide a promising platform for realizing novel quantum phases driven by spin-orbital exchange interactions, as described by the Kugel-Khomskii model. Spinel vanadates, in which orbital degrees of freedom remain active, exhibit structural and magnetic transitions accompanied by orbital ordering, but the nature of the orbital state in MnV$_2$O$_4$ remains under debate. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with an effective spin-orbital model to address this problem. We show that a significant trigonal crystal field is present in high-temperature cubic phase and plays an essential role in determining the low-energy degrees of freedom. Based on the resulting parameters, we construct an effective Hamiltonian beyond the conventional dominant-hopping approximation and demonstrate that subdominant hopping processes strongly modify the spin-orbital exchange interactions. As a result, the system stabilizes a two-in/two-out magnetic configuration featuring spin canting and intertwined dipole-quadrupole orbital order.

papers.title: Guidelines for band gap opening in graphene superlattices with periodic {\pi}-vacancy distribution
papers.summary: Periodic $\pi$-vacancies in graphene superlattices (GSLs) provide a symmetry-based route to band-gap opening in graphene by modifying the $\pi$-band dispersion. However, the symmetry conditions that determine whether a vacancy motif can open a band gap remain unclear. Here, we investigate periodic $\pi$-vacancy GSLs using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model with one $p_z$ orbital per carbon site to identify the symmetry requirements for gap opening. $\pi$-vacancies, representing functionalized, substituted, or missing carbon sites, are modeled as site deletions in the $\pi$ basis, with all hopping matrix elements to and from the deleted sites set to zero. We focus on $\pi$-vacancy motifs with $C_2$ and $C_3$ point-group symmetry. A $3n \times 3n$ GSL, where $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ is the integer scaling factor multiplying the honeycomb primitive-cell vectors, folds $K$ and $K'$ to $\Gamma$ and can therefore open a band gap. For $C_3$-type vacancies, the Dirac cones remain pinned at high-symmetry points and thus stay at $\Gamma$ in folded $3n$ GSLs. In contrast, $C_2$-type vacancies that reduce the global point group of the GSL to $D_{2h}$ by preserving a pair of perpendicular mirror symmetries, $\sigma_v \perp \sigma_d$, can also constrain the Dirac cones to $\Gamma$. When the $\sigma_v$ and $\sigma_d$ mirror planes are absent, the cones are allowed to shift away from $\Gamma$ to $(\pm \Delta q,\pm \Delta q)$ in the $3n$ superlattice.

papers.title: Anomalous Transverse Thomson Effect
papers.summary: We formulate the anomalous transverse Thomson effect (ATTE), the long-missing Thomson counterpart of the anomalous Hall and anomalous Nernst effects. Its coefficient is not unique but depends on the electrical boundary condition: $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(j)}$, defined for a spatially uniform imposed current density, and $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$, defined for equipotential electrodes. Both are fully determined by the total anomalous Nernst coefficient (ANC) and its temperature dependence, while $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$ acquires an additional contribution from the temperature dependence of the longitudinal resistivity. This relation is model independent within local linear response and applies to the total ANC regardless of whether its microscopic origin is intrinsic or extrinsic. Using a massive Dirac model for Fe$_3$Sn$_2$, we show that Berry curvature near the gapped Dirac cones enhances the ANC-related contributions to $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$. In the low-temperature limit, both $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(j)}/S_{xy}^{\rm A}$ and $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}/S_{xy}^{\rm A}$ approach a value of three. We further extract $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$ from reported experimental data for CoS\(_2\), Co\(_3\)Sn\(_2\)S\(_2\) and CeCrGe\(_3\); for CeCrGe$_3$ it reaches approximately -20 $\mu V/K$, and we estimate the maximum achievable cold-side heat current density to assess its cooling potential. Because the ATTE can be evaluated directly from existing ANC and longitudinal resistivity data, it is readily testable without additional equipment or measurements.

papers.title: Cycle affinity and winding localize eigenvalues of Markov generators
papers.summary: The complex eigenvalues of Markov generators govern oscillatory properties of relaxation, autocorrelation, and linear response. We show that these eigenvalues are localized by nonequilibrium cycles of the generator, thus revealing a fundamental tradeoff between thermodynamic driving, oscillation, and decay of eigenmodes. Specifically, we prove that each complex eigenvalue is confined to a region determined by the cycle affinity and the eigenvector ``winding number'' of some nonequilibrium cycle. In discrete and continuous unicyclic systems, we also demonstrate that the winding number is determined by the ordered eigenvalue index, yielding new thermodynamic bounds on the slowest and fastest relaxation modes. In discrete multicyclic systems, our approach unifies and extends several previous inequalities and proves the Uhl--Seifert ellipse conjecture.

papers.title: First-Principles Study of Fe Adsorption and Its Effects on the Mechanical and Electrical Properties of Monolayer and Bilayer Biphenylene Networks
papers.summary: BPN is a 2D carbon allotrope that exhibits promising potential for applications across a wide range of fields. In this work, we systematically investigated the adsorption characteristics of Fe atoms on monolayer and bilayer BPN using first-principles calculations. Structural optimization and adsorption energy analysis reveal that, for monolayer BPN, the adsorption strength gradually enhances with increasing Fe coverage, indicating a strengthening of Fe-substrate interactions. An Fe/C ratio of 50% corresponds approximately to completion of the first Fe adsorption layer on the BPN surface. For bilayer BPN, the energetically preferred adsorption site for Fe atom is located at the center of the interlayer four-membered ring, with an average adsorption energy of -4.3 eV. Mechanical properties are further evaluated for pristine and Fe-decorated BPN. The results demonstrate that monolayer and bilayer BPN possess relatively high in-plane Young's and shear moduli, indicative of excellent in-plane mechanical stability. For monolayer BPN, Fe adsorption has only a limited effect on the in-plane mechanical response at low coverages, whereas a noticeable enhancement in stiffness emerges at higher Fe loadings. In contrast, the out-of-plane mechanical response of bilayer BPN is significantly affected by Fe incorporation. The effective out-of-plane elastic constant C33 of pristine bilayer BPN is calculated to be 24.59 GPa, indicating relatively weak interlayer interactions and facile deformation along the out-of-plane direction. Notably, this property can be substantially enhanced by interlayer Fe adsorption, with C33 increasing dramatically to 515.63 GPa upon an Fe/C ratio of 25 %. The transport calculations reveal pronounced anisotropy in the conductivity normalized by the relaxation time {\sigma} / {\tau}, with markedly different values along the two in-plane crystallographic directions.

papers.title: Universality in the target arrival statistics of non-conservative search processes
papers.summary: Stochastic search processes in which agents are continuously inserted into and removed from a target search domain are fundamental to a wide class of physical and artificial systems. The theory of such non-conservative search processes is, however, much less developed than for search processes with a fixed number of agents. Recent work on the non-conservative case has characterized the fastest first-passage time (FPT) to a target, after which the search process is terminated. Here we consider the complementary problem of continuous arrival statistics to a target. In particular, we derive the full time-dependent distribution of target arrivals, which we use to show that the inter-arrival time distribution is exactly exponential in steady-state regardless of the underlying search process. Thus, counterintuitively, the arrival statistics of non-conservative search are both universal and much simpler than sequential search-and-capture processes involving a fixed number of agents. Our methods also yield an exact expression for the fastest FPT distribution with time-dependent insertion, thereby generalizing previous work on fixed-rate insertion for non-conservative search. Altogether these results have major implications for target resource accumulation, wherein the delivery of resources is counter-balanced by their downstream consumption.

papers.title: Frustration induced dimensional reduction and coexistence of long and short-range magnetic order in NdCl$_{3}$
papers.summary: The phenomenon of frustration greatly enriches the accessible physics of quantum magnets. With this in mind we study the magnetism of \NC using a combination of bulk properties measurements and neutron scattering techniques. The low-temperature heat capacity reveals two magnetic transitions at $T_{N1}$ = 270 mK and $T_{N2}$ = 180 mK. However, much of the magnetic entropy is released above $T_{N1}$, manifesting as a broad peak centered at $T^{*} \approx$ 450 mK. A similar broad peak is observed in the magnetic susceptibility, which possesses a clear anisotropy; this data can be well fit using a 1-dimensional XXZ model, yielding an antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor exchange $J_{NN}$ = -0.962(2) K and exchange anisotropy close to the Ising limit. Single crystal elastic neutron scattering reveals highly anisotropic magnetic diffuse scattering above $T_{N1}$, confirming that quasi-one-dimensional, short-range, antiferromagnetic order is the origin of the broad peak in the heat capacity and magnetic susceptibility. Magnetic Bragg peaks characterized by a $\vec{k}$ = ($0$ $0$ $\frac{1}{2}$) propagation vector emerge below $T_{N1}$. Interestingly, the magnetic diffuse scattering persists for $T_{N2} < T < T_{N1}$, indicating a regime of coexisting short and long-range order. The magnetic Bragg peaks exhibit an additional increase in intensity below $T_{N2}$ with no change in $\vec{k}$. Concomitantly, the diffuse scattering disappears indicating the attainment of full long-range order. While the precise nature of the ordered magnetic ground state remains unresolved, the observed magnetic scattering indicates predominate $c$-axis moments with a small $ab$-plane component. We propose that the quasi-one-dimensional behavior and the coexistence of short and long-range order are driven by frustration of exchange interactions with significant anisotropy.

papers.title: Contrasting $\Gamma$- and K-Valley Moir\'e Physics in Twisted Monolayer/Bilayer WSe$_2$
papers.summary:
Electronic orbital character plays a central role in determining electronic correlations, spin-orbit coupling, dimensionality, and ultimately the quantum phases of condensed-matter systems. Two-dimensional moir'e materials have emerged as highly tunable platforms for exploring correlated phenomena, but the role of orbital degrees of freedom remains largely unexplored. Here, we identify twisted monolayer/bilayer WSe$_2$ as a platform in which displacement-field tuning enables moir'e physics to be realized in both the $K$ and $\Gamma$ valleys. The distinct orbital characters of these valleys give rise to contrasting correlated phases at moir'e filling factors $
u=1$ and $
u=1/3$. At $
u=1$, the $K$-valley state is a weak insulator, consistent with an antiferromagnetic state near a van Hove singularity in the intermediate-coupling regime, similar to that observed in twisted bilayer WSe$_2$. In contrast, the $\Gamma$-valley state exhibits a pronounced Pomeranchuk effect, consistent with proximity to a Mott transition. At $
u=1/3$, the $K$ valley hosts a robust generalized Wigner crystal, whereas the $\Gamma$-valley state lies near the crystallization boundary and again exhibits a Pomeranchuk effect, with localization enhanced by increasing temperature or magnetic field. Our work highlights the importance of orbital character in defining quantum phases in moir'e systems, and identify the $\Gamma$ valley as a promising platform for exploring correlated phenomena near quantum phase transitions, where competing phases and enhanced fluctuations may give rise to unconventional phases.

papers.title: HPHT growth of centimeter-sized cubic boron nitride crystals
papers.summary: Single crystals of cubic boron nitride (cBN) exceeding 10 mm in size were grown by the high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) temperature-gradient method using a Ni-Cr-based solvent catalyst. Compared with the previously reported maximum crystal size of approximately 3 mm, this improvement was achieved by maintaining a stable precursor flux during one week of growth at a source temperature of 1950 {\deg}C. In contrast to diamonds, which were grown with the same HPHT cell and showed nearly isometric shapes, the cBN crystals had elongated shapes. We attribute this cBN morphology to a localized growth near the BN source due to the relatively low effective diffusivity of boron and nitrogen species in the metallic solvent.

papers.title: Weakly non-linear creep of amorphous polymers near their glass transition, comparisons between models and experiment
papers.summary: The non-linear mechanics of amorphous polymers near the glass transition reveals a stress-induced acceleration of stress relaxation of nanometric sub-units. Recent theoretical work predicts that the local acceleration within these nano-domains should scale as the exponential of the squared local stress, a behavior now supported by experiments. However, this local dynamics has some complex consequences on the macroscopic mechanical response, as dynamical heterogeneities generate complex stress and strain fields in polymers close to the glass transition. In this study we consider the non-linear creep of an amorphous polymer near its glass transition and evaluate the relation between local and global acceleration and the emerging load-carrying structure, by comparing experimental data with predictions of three models of increasing complexity: a two-states (2S) model, a self-consistent (SC) model and a finite-element (FEM) model. The experimentally observed trend of accelerated creep under increasing applied stress is reproduced by the SC and FEM models, while the 2S model overestimates stress localization. The macroscopic, homogenized acceleration is predicted to be close to the microscopic one, albeit with an apparent yield stress that depends on compliance. The FEM model evidences the development of a load carrying sub-structure that occupies a small fraction of the total material volume driven by the interaction of sub-domains. This work shows that complexity and heterogeneity emerge due to non-linear interactions and that their adequate representation is essential for predicting the macroscopic mechanical response of amorphous polymers near their glass transition.

papers.title: Quenched complexity of marginal states in the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin glass
papers.summary: The number of metastable states of a random corrugated landscape controls what dynamics, inference and learning can reach. In the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model these states are marginal, and counting them requires breaking the BRST symmetry. So far only the annealed complexity was known, predicting states below equilibrium. We compute the quenched complexity function with a two-group Ansatz and one-step replica symmetry breaking. It branches continuously off the annealed curve at its instability point and vanishes near the Parisi free energy, while the soft mode turns toward orthogonality to the magnetization.

papers.title: Vestigial chirality from fluctuating loop currents on the kagome lattice
papers.summary: Multicomponent order can melt in stages, leaving a composite order after its primary constituents become short ranged. We study this possibility for commensurate three-$Q$ loop-current order on the kagome lattice. Large-scale cluster and parallel-tempering Monte Carlo simulations reveal direct and two-stage melting regimes in an effective fixed-amplitude sign model. In the latter regime, translation-sector domain walls proliferate before chirality-changing walls, restoring lattice translational symmetry while preserving long-range time-reversal-odd order. The primary $M$-point correlations are short ranged in this intermediate phase. The two-stage regime begins when the lowest-energy chirality-changing wall is only about $12$--$13\%$ more costly than a same-chirality translation wall. Finite-size scaling of a stable amplitude-resolved Ginzburg--Landau theory shows that the phase survives amplitude relaxation. Our results establish a quantitative domain-wall criterion for vestigial loop-current order and a fluctuation route to time-reversal symmetry breaking without long-range loop-current Bragg order. This separation provides a possible thermodynamic framework for time-reversal-odd responses recently reported above the critical temperature for conventional charge-density-wave ordering in kagome metals.

papers.title: Ergodicity in a hole-doped Anderson spin insulator
papers.summary: An interacting many-body system being localized in the presence of disorder can fail to serve as its own bath. In an electronic system, the charge and spin degrees of freedom can act as thermal baths for each other. In this paper, we study the stability of an Anderson insulator in the spin sector with respect to charge doping. We consider one-dimensional two-component fermions in a lattice with large onsite repulsion ($t-J_{XX}$ model) and with a single hole in a random magnetic field. In the absence of the hole the spin sector is localized in arbitrarily weak random magnetic fields. We argue that a single hole thermalizes the spin chain in the weak disorder limit. In this regime our numerical results indicate ergodicity of the system as a whole and delocalization of the hole. At larger magnetic fields the hole eventually localizes with a finite localization length, and the Anderson spin insulator is restored.

papers.title: Uniform-Charge-Density $d$-Wave Superconductivity in the Pure $t$-$J$ Model at $1/8$ Doping on an Infinite Cylinder
papers.summary: The ground state of the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at $1/8$ hole doping has been the subject of a long-standing controversy, with conflicting numerical reports of stripe order versus superconductivity. Here, we address this debate using the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) method, which optimizes the wave function directly in the thermodynamic limit along the cylinder axis and eliminates the boundary pinning effects that can arise in finite-cylinder calculations. On an infinite cylinder of circumference $L_y = 8$, we find a uniform-charge-density $d$-wave superconducting ground state with quasi-long-range pairing correlations. The dominant pairing occurs at zero center-of-mass momentum, while no sizable finite-momentum pairing component is detected. Twisted-boundary-condition calculations reveal a finite superconducting phase stiffness, with the order-parameter phase winding smoothly to follow the applied flux, providing an independent probe of the robustness of the superconductivity. Moreover, both charge and spin correlations decay rapidly, with no signatures of long-range stripe or magnetic order, in contrast to an $L_y=6$ cylinder at $1/6$ doping where the same method readily identifies stripe order. Our results provide methodologically distinct evidence in the long-standing stripe--superconductivity debate in the pure $t$-$J$ model and reveal uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in a minimal model of doped Mott insulators.

papers.title: Classification of topological phases of matter in stochastic systems
papers.summary: Topological phases of matter support edge states protected from random perturbations, and the identification of the discrete non-spatial symmetries and dimensions that support such phases was systematically developed for quantum systems and analogous platforms. While topological phases were also discovered in stochastic systems and posited as mechanisms for key biochemical processes, a classification consistent with their Markovian constraints remains lacking, impeding generalization to new scenarios. To address this, we develop new methods including a new homotopy approach, real-space invariants and a redefinition of the point gap to classify both transient and steady states. We find robust transient states in two symmetry classes, no symmetry and pseudo-Hermiticity respectively, while topological steady states are expected only in systems without symmetry. We identify the dimensions with non-trivial phases and their group structure, creating a rigorous framework for predicting robust behavior in active and living matter.

papers.title: Pressure induced structural transitions, coordination crossover, and optoelectronic response in divalent metavanadate CaV$_2$O$_6$
papers.summary: High-pressure synchrotron X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, photoluminescence (PL), and UV-Vis absorption measurements were carried out on the divalent metavanadate CaV$_2$O$_6$ up to 31 GPa at room temperature. Ambient CaV$_2$O$_6$ crystallizes in a centrosymmetric pseudo-brannerite monoclinic structure ($C2/m$), where vanadium atoms reside in fivefold-coordinated VO$_5$ trigonal bipyramids. Under hydrostatic compression, the system undergoes a structural phase transition starting at $\sim$1 GPa to a lower-symmetry, non-centrosymmetric monoclinic phase ($C2$), which becomes the single stable phase above 5.2 GPa. This transition involves an increase in vanadium coordination from VO$_5$ bipyramids to edge-sharing distorted VO$_6$ octahedra. High-pressure Raman scattering corroborates the structural phase boundaries, exhibiting mode softening ($\gamma_3 = -0.42$, $\gamma_9 = -0.46$) within the mixed-phase regime (1.0 - 4.4 GPa) and sharp anomalies in mode frequencies and linewidths across 5.2 GPa. The optical measurements show complete PL quenching near 1 GPa due to non-radiative recombination pathways introduced by local polyhedral distortions, alongside a non-monotonic evolution of the indirect optical band gap. Above 20 GPa, an anomaly in polyhedral distortion and internal strain drives an isosymmetric structural modification within the $C2$ phase, marked by an alteration in bulk compressibility and stabilization of the optical gap. Comparative high-pressure band-gap measurements on the sister compound MgV$_2$O$_6$ validate the explicit coupling between cation coordination changes and optoelectronic response in divalent metavanadates.

papers.title: Closed analytical form of many-body free volume and thermodynamics of monodisperse hard disks
papers.summary: The hard disk model is a fundamental reference system for excluded volume physics, liquid structure, and 2D ordering. Yet, despite its apparent simplicity, an analytical formulation of its thermodynamics has remained difficult because the free volume available to disks centers has a highly nontrivial many-body geometry. Here we show that this geometry admits a closed and exact representation: for any given hard disk configuration, the free volume can be analytically expressed through intersection areas of up to five exclusion disks. This provides a direct geometrical route from particle coordinates to the configurational partition function and entropy. We prove that the N disk partition function factorizes into a product of conditional free volumes and identify its two limiting asymptotic forms: the low density fluid regime controlled by extensive cavities and the high density fluid regime controlled by intensive private cells. Using the geometric measures computed from representative equilibrium particle configurations, the resulting theory reproduces the established hard disk equation of state over almost the entire density range up to close packing. At intermediate densities, the analysis reveals a mixed fluid regime in which localized caged defects provide an additional configurational entropy within the density interval preceding liquid hexatic coexistence. Finally, the five disk intersection area is shown to be a sensitive local scalar measure of hexagonal ordering, complementing the orientational order parameter and emphasizing the central role of many-body correlations.

papers.title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
papers.summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are transforming atomistic simulations by accessing unprecedented length and time scales. While pretrained equivariant graph neural networks achieve robust zero-shot performance for near-equilibrium properties across broad chemical spaces, their translation to complex materials dynamics remains fundamentally challenged by out-of-distribution reactive states, representation biases, and computational scaling limits. In this Review, we examine how physics-driven specialization extends the applicability of MLIPs to complex dynamical systems. We systematically evaluate the structural trade-offs in MLIP design: the undersampling of highly strained configurations, the prohibitive computational overhead of high-order message-passing architectures, and the necessity of nonlocal interactions for open and field-coupled systems. Through four demanding application contexts - electrified interfaces, compositionally fluctuating open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture - we establish a framework for observable-specific validation. Highlighting the complementary roles of universal foundation models and task-specific potentials, we emphasize that targeted adaptations must be rigorously benchmarked against intended observables. We conclude with a roadmap for developing physically consistent, hardware-aware force fields that seamlessly connect electronic-structure accuracy to macroscopic materials phenomena.

papers.title: Ultrasound and Magnetic Resonance Elastography of the Neck: Biomechanical Basis, Clinical Applications and Methodological Challenges
papers.summary: Many neck disorders, from chronic neck pain and headache to thyroid and nodal malignancy and radiation-induced fibrosis, both arise from and alter the mechanical properties of neck tissues, yet clinical assessment still relies on morphology, palpation and symptoms. Ultrasound and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) now allow these properties to be measured in vivo, but the neck literature differs widely in methodology and remains dispersed across modalities and tissues. This review brings together the biomechanical basis of neck tissue behavior, the clinical conditions that alter it, and the principles and applications of ultrasound elastography and MRE in the neck. We show that ultrasound elastography has demonstrated diagnostic value for thyroid nodules and cervical lymph nodes, while neck MRE has been shown to be feasible but remains at an early stage. Across both modalities, reported values depend strongly on fiber orientation, posture, muscle activation and acquisition conditions. We therefore propose reporting recommendations and discuss how measurements beyond stiffness, including anisotropy, viscosity and nonlinearity, could improve disease management and inform computational models of the neck.

papers.title: On the Performance of Randomly Generated Codebooks in Near-Field Communications
papers.summary: Near-field communication with large antenna arrays requires beamforming techniques that account for spherical wavefront effects. While predefined codebooks are widely used in multiple-antenna wireless systems, the performance of randomly generated codebooks in the near-field region has not been investigated. In this work, we study four randomly generated codebooks for near-field communications: random vector quantization (RVQ), random phase (RP), random far-field (RFF), and random near-field (RNF) codebooks. We use the known RVQ gain distribution as a benchmark. For RP, we derive a large-array bulk approximation and characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RNF, we characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RFF, we derive an analytical approximation for the maximum achievable beamforming gain when far-field beams are used to serve near-field users, along with the corresponding maximizing far-field direction. We also analyze the maximum-gain scaling with codebook size. Monte Carlo simulations verify the analytical results and show that RVQ and RP degrade significantly as the array size increases, while RNF achieves the most favorable high-gain scaling. RFF can outperform RVQ and RP for finite codebook sizes, but its maximum gain saturates below one due to the phase mismatch between the far-field beams and the near-field channel. These results show how codebook structure, array size, and codebook size affect random beamforming performance in the near-field.

papers.title: Simultaneous Direct and Indirect Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications
papers.summary: This paper introduces an enhanced channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Considering the presence of both the direct link from the base station (BS) to the user equipment (UE) and the indirect link \textit{via} the RIS, we formulate a tensor-based receiver for joint direct and indirect channel estimation called the TenDICE algorithm. The proposed receiver relies on an extended parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) tensor model for the received pilot signals, from which the involved (direct and indirect link) channels are estimated using a simple alternating least squares scheme. The proposed TenDICE method is compared with the state-of-the-art least squares (LS) method, Khatri-Rao factorization (KRF) method, enhanced trilinear alternating least squares (E-TALS), and the theoretical Cram\'er-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based on normalized mean square error (NMSE) and spectral efficiency (SE). The proposed TenDICE outperforms the LS and E-TALS methods and performs similarly to the KRF methods while estimating the direct channel.

papers.title: Minimum Bounding Sets for N-1-1 Branch Contingencies Under Thermal and Voltage Limits in Linear Network Models
papers.summary: N-1-1 contingency analysis studies the loss of one element followed by system adjustments and the loss of a second. The number of contingency pairs increases quadratically with the number of applicable elements, and traditional ranking-based screening methods cannot guarantee that omitted pairs are bounded. This paper determines the minimum bounding set of two-branch-outage pairs: the smallest set that can reproduce the worst value of every violated thermal and voltage limit of a linear network model. In the DC model, effects of an outage pair can be quantified by the extent of the coupling between the outages. The paper measures this by the cosine between the two outages in the network's cycle space, with a bound that splits into one term per outage and is within a near-ideal factor of $\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}$. This argument extends to every linear model in which an outage subtracts a positive semi-definite low-rank term from a symmetric positive definite matrix, with a tight bound and a collapse test. A model with voltage magnitudes is extracted by performing one Newton step on the energy function of the lossless network in rectangular coordinates. A best-first search built on these bounds reproduced brute force on public systems of up to 2{,}869 buses with 130 to 3{,}800 times fewer pair evaluations for flows and 170 to 23{,}700 times fewer for voltages. Gaps in translation to nonlinear models are explored on the IEEE 118-bus system.

papers.title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
papers.summary: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a one-time symbolic phase, the runtime bus-type projection overhead is entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The framework is realized in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 24.4-30.1x faster than the MATPOWER- style baseline and 6.0-7.8x faster than the Schafer-Braun optimized assembly. End-to-end, the grid-level solve time is 11.7x-154.3x faster than pandapower 3.5.4 with Numba, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. Compared with the native C++ LightSim2Grid 1.0.0, grid-level performance is comparable on IEEE 39 and 1.3x-1.8x faster on IEEE 118 and the PEGASE systems. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.

papers.title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification
papers.summary: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.

papers.title: ROAM: Reinforcement Learning Optimized Adaptive Moving Target Defense for Smart Grid
papers.summary: Smart grids rely on distributed phasor measurement units (PMUs) and wide-area communication networks whose data-acquisition pipelines are vulnerable to stealthy false data injection (FDI) attacks that evade conventional bad-data detection (BDD). Moving target defense (MTD) counters this exposure by continuously remapping sensor identities, but existing schemes apply static or pre-scheduled randomization and are each constrained by a single failure mode: seed-based methods are fast yet fragile to key compromise, while machine learning (ML) based prediction methods are resilient yet incur prohibitive latency. Neither adapts its randomization to live threat evidence. This paper presents ROAM, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) driven MTD framework in which a deep Q-network (DQN) agent continuously re-optimizes the sensor-to-ID mapping at the aggregation layer. At each decision step, the agent selects the deception coverage, flags the specific sensors to remap, and sets the split of the remapped sensors between seed-based and ML-prediction-based recovery, without modifying PMU hardware and while preserving IEEE C37.118 compatibility. On held-out BDD-compliant FDI scenarios across the IEEE 14-, 57-, and 118- bus systems, ROAM keeps the percentage of stealthy attacks below 3% while sustaining detection rates above 93%. Against an adaptive soft actor-critic (SAC) attacker that observes the defender's configuration, ROAM keeps stealthy attacks below 2.6% with detection above 92%. Hardware-in-the-loop testing on an OPAL-RT platform confirms real-time feasibility, with sub-18ms average shuffle execution and an average reshuffle blind window of 2.6% of the 3-s decision cycle.

papers.title: Generative Control of Time-Modulated Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Scalable Directional Modulation
papers.summary: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces (TM-IRS) achieve directional modulation by switching their elements on and off at designed instants and durations, so that an undistorted signal reaches the intended user while appearing scrambled elsewhere. We propose a Flow Matching (FM)-based generative framework that designs these parameters for strong scrambling and reliable reception simultaneously. For orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, we introduce a physics-informed reward that maximizes the time-modulation harmonic energy radiated in the null space of the legitimate-user response, subject to a minimum per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), without requiring knowledge of adversary directions. Unlike prior generative flow network (GFlowNet) approaches, which assign discretized parameters sequentially, the FM model generates complete continuous configurations jointly, decoupling the generation depth from the number of elements and accelerating training. It also learns a distribution over configurations that can be resampled to vary the scrambling pattern. Numerical results show that, compared with a GFlowNet baseline, the proposed approach reduces the time to training loss near-saturation by $99.4\%$ on average for $3{\times}3$ to $12{\times}12$ surfaces, attains higher final rewards, scales to $80{\times}80$, and confines the low-symbol-error region more tightly around the legitimate user.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Adaptive Iterative Covariance Steering for Small-Body Proximity Operations
papers.summary: Autonomous small-body proximity operations require continuous-thrust guidance under uncertain gravity, solar-radiation pressure (SRP), and stochastic disturbances. We combine iterative covariance steering (iCS) with $L_1$ distributionally robust adaptive control ($L_1$-DRAC) to provide risk-aware collision avoidance despite mismatch between the nominal planning model and the true dynamics. Iterative covariance steering plans a nominal feedback policy satisfying distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk keep-out constraints, while $L_1$-DRAC compensates for dynamics uncertainty and bounds the residual distributional mismatch through a Wasserstein radius used by the planner. In $\mathbf{1000}$ paired Monte Carlo trials with gravity, SRP, and diffusion mismatch, $L_1$-DRAC adaptive control reduces the keep-out violation rate from $\mathbf{32.7\%}$ to $\mathbf{0.2\%}$ and the physical collision rate from $\mathbf{16.4\%}$ to zero, without actuator saturation.

papers.title: Closed-loop domain generation enhances battery health diagnosis
papers.summary: Reliable electrode-level degradation diagnosis is essential for accurate health estimation and non-destructive monitoring in advanced battery management. Diagnosis models developed under controlled laboratory conditions can fail when operating conditions change, while acquiring sufficient full-lifespan data in new target domains remains prohibitively time-consuming and practically unfeasible. Here, we propose a closed-loop domain generation framework to enable cross-domain battery health diagnosis under dynamic conditions. Physics-constrained domain generation is achieved through Variational Autoencoder-based latent extrapolation, which maps the source data and few-shot early-life target domain data into a shared latent space and generates cross-domain samples within physical boundaries. Bayesian optimization closes the generation-diagnosis loop by automatically calibrating the sampling, latent regularization, extrapolation, perturbation, and generation-volume hyperparameters using leakage-free development validation, thereby strictly excluding later-life target data from optimization and ensuring the quality and quantity of generated data. Numerical results demonstrate that, across four cross-domain cases, the proposed framework achieves average root mean square errors of 1.53%, 2.15%, and 2.02% for positive electrode active material loss, negative electrode active material loss, and lithium inventory loss, respectively, whereas traditional methods suffer from notably higher errors or even complete failure. This framework provides a general pathway for onboard and physics-consistent electrode-level degradation diagnosis, independent of downstream diagnosis models.

papers.title: Fast-DeePC: Fast Data-Enabled Predictive Control using Soft-constrained Scheme
papers.summary: Data-enabled predictive control (DeePC) replaces the explicit system model of model predictive control with a data-driven predictor built directly from recorded input-output trajectories, but the original hard-equality formulation keeps its coordinate vector as an online decision variable whose size grows with the offline data length, so the online problem grows more expensive as more data is used to enrich the behavioral representation. This article proposes Fast-DeePC, a framework which relaxes this consistency relation into the control objective with a quadratic ridge on the coordinate vector in place of the customary sparsity-promoting penalty, admitting a closed-form, offline elimination of the coordinate vector and reducing the online problem to a fixed-size box-constrained quadratic program solved by a structure-exploiting interior-point method. On identical soft quadratically regularized problems, the result matches a general-purpose solver's solution and is up to two orders of magnitude faster.

papers.title: SecFD-FL: Frequency-Decoupled Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation for Charging Load Forecasting in Internet of Electric Vehicles
papers.summary: Accurate charging load forecasting is essential for the reliability and efficiency of the Internet of Electric Vehicles (IoEV), yet it is challenging on two fronts: charging demand is highly stochastic, and the data collected by distributed sensors is privacy-sensitive. Although federated learning (FL) preserves data privacy, collaborative training still remains vulnerable to an honest-but-curious server that can invert shared model updates to reconstruct private data. To address both data volatility and privacy concerns, we propose SecFD-FL, a frequency-decoupled federated learning framework for IoEV comprising: 1) a dual-stream gated recurrent unit (GRU) network that separately models short-term and long-term charging load volatility, and 2) a lightweight secure aggregation layer for privacy preservation. Specifically, the secure aggregation layer employs a zero-sum additive masking protocol that perturbs each client's upload with high-variance noise, preventing the server from reconstructing private data while preserving the exact aggregate. Extensive experiments have been conducted on both EV-level and charging station-level using real datasets. The experiment results show that SecFD-FL reduces global RMSE by up to 60% over centralized baselines, achieving Jain's fairness up to 0.991 across clients, and reduces DLG-attack reconstruction correlation by 8 times to 15 times relative to FedAvg -- all with no additional per-round communication cost beyond a one-time key exchange.

papers.title: Self-Calibration DOA Estimation for Moving Dilated Arrays with Gain and Phase Errors
papers.summary: Moving dilated arrays (MDAs) can increase the uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs) while alleviating mutual coupling, but their performance is susceptible to unknown gain and phase errors (GPEs). To deal with this problem, we investigate self-calibration direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for MDAs with unknown GPEs. First, multi-position observations are phase aligned to construct an equivalent virtual array with an enlarged aperture. Next, the motion-induced relationships among the GPEs are exploited to establish explicit calibration constraints. By leveraging the orthogonality between the steering vectors and the noise subspace, the joint estimation of the DOAs and GPEs is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. To solve this problem, a two-stage alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. In the first stage, the GPEs are estimated in closed form with the DOAs fixed. In the second stage, the estimated GPEs are used to calibrate the covariance matrix, after which the DOAs are refined using the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To obtain reliable initial estimates, a rotational invariance-like (RIL) initialization method is further developed by exploiting two translated virtual subarrays with identical GPEs. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the theoretical performance limit of the considered system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges reliably and achieves accurate DOA estimation under different array apertures, numbers of snapshots, GPE levels, and numbers of sources.

papers.title: E3-System: Expressive EmoData, Explicitly Controllable, Easy-to-Use TTS
papers.summary: Recent zero-shot Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems can clone unseen speakers, yet controllable expressiveness remains limited by a gap between semantic intent and acoustic realization. Text descriptions offer a natural control interface but provide weak acoustic grounding, whereas speech style prompts provide concrete prosody but entangle style with the prompt speaker's timbre. To bridge this gap, we propose E3-System, a unified intent-to-speech framework for expressive zero-shot TTS that couples three requirements: Expressive style modeling, Explicit timbre-style control, and Easy-to-use natural-language interaction. Given a target speaker and either a natural-language style description or a speech style prompt, E3-System generates expressive speech while preserving the target timbre. The key idea is to close the full control loop: building a large expressive style space, grounding user intent into usable acoustic style references, and synthesizing speech with disentangled timbre and style. To realize this loop, EmoData provides a thousand-hour multilingual emotional speech dataset, Style-RAG grounds text descriptions into high-quality acoustic style prompts from these data, and Dual-TTS transfers the grounded style to arbitrary target speakers through VC-augmented timbre-style disentanglement. Experiments show that E3-System achieves strong speech quality, speaker preservation, and explicit expressive controllability.

papers.title: Virtual Transmission Lines from Data Center Workload Migration: Coordinated Multi-Year Transmission Expansion Planning
papers.summary: The rapid growth of electricity demand from AI data centers is creating a dual mismatch in power systems: a temporal mismatch between fast-rising demand and slow transmission expansion, and a spatial mismatch between concentrated data-center loads and geographically dispersed renewable resources. These mismatches can exacerbate transmission congestion, resulting in unserved data-center load and renewable-energy curtailment. This study models geographic workload migration as a virtual transmission line (VTL) that changes nodal data-center demand without transferring physical electricity. A mixed-integer linear programming model is then developed to co-optimize multi-year candidate-line construction and workload migration, subject to construction delays, renewable-energy curtailment, unserved data-center load, workload-balance requirements, communication-bandwidth constraints, and link-latency limits. The model is evaluated over an eight-year planning horizon on a modified IEEE 14-bus system. The results show that coordinating VTL with physical transmission expansion reduces total system cost, unserved data-center load, and renewable-energy curtailment while alleviating transmission congestion. VTL-aware planning also requires one fewer candidate line than build-only planning. However, VTL alone cannot meet system demand and does not eliminate the need for physical transmission reinforcement. Sensitivity analysis indicates that VTL provides the greatest value when transfer capacity is tight, construction costs are high, load growth is rapid, and data-center flexibility is greater. Additional validation on the IEEE 118-bus system over a five-year planning horizon shows that coordinated planning retains its cost and reliability benefits while reducing physical expansion requirements.

papers.title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count
papers.summary: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.

papers.title: Stochastic Finite-Transition Learning and Exploration for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
papers.summary: Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory. Common generative methods, such as diffusion and flow, typically learn fine-grained local dynamics whose integration defines this global mapping, hence requiring many network evaluations at inference. Existing few-step sampling approaches can lower computational burden by approximating large transformations from local dynamics, albeit at the expense of reconstruction fidelity. FLEX-MRI instead partitions recovery into a small number of finite intervals between retained states defined by progressive changes in k-space support, and directly learns the reconstruction change across each interval. Because such finite transitions can admit multiple plausible outcomes, FLEX-MRI combines support-relaxed finite-transition learning with stochastic exploration. During training, randomized k-space sampling masks define finite-transition targets with varying support, while the prediction loss remains unrestricted by each individual mask. At inference, FLEX-MRI perturbs a random subset of currently estimated k-space coefficients, allowing the learned predictor to stochastically explore alternative transition paths. Each predicted state is then reconciled with the acquired measurements through data consistency. We theoretically show that this stochastic exploration induces nonzero transition-level variation through the learned recovery map and data consistency without requiring an auxiliary generative sampler. Experiments on multi-coil MRI datasets show that FLEX-MRI outperforms competing methods while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to few-step baselines.

papers.title: LLM-Assisted Hierarchical Interference Control for Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks
papers.summary: Time-varying aggregate interference from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites challenges terrestrial-network (TN) protection, whereas conservative control degrades LEO quality of service (QoS). This letter proposes a hierarchical framework combining geometry-based interference estimation, QoS-constrained power control, adaptive energy detection, large language model (LLM)-assisted candidate ranking, stay-or-switch decisions, and target-band selection, with deterministic verification. The current band is retained only when both spectrum-hole and power-feasibility conditions hold, with periodic reevaluation. Over a 300-s horizon with 0.5-s sampling, the proposed method keeps the aggregate INR from exceeding the $-12.2$~dB threshold and achieves a time-averaged mean LEO-link rate of $320.97$~Mbps with $100\%$ QoS satisfaction. It markedly outperforms power-only and satellite-muting in jointly protecting the TN and preserving LEO QoS.

papers.title: Extended Neighborhood Message Passing for Inference in Loopy Factor Graphs
papers.summary: Belief propagation (BP) is widely used for inference on probabilistic graphical models but often suffers from non-convergence and poor accuracy on loopy factor graphs, yielding inexact variance estimates in the Gaussian case. Generalized BP (GBP) improves accuracy but relies on manual design or application-specific heuristics for region-graph construction. We propose extended neighborhood message passing (ENMP), which automatically constructs extended neighborhoods of variable nodes from the bipartite factor graph topology, capturing loop-induced correlations without manual region design. The framework applies to general distributions on factor graphs with a tunable accuracy-complexity trade-off. In the exact regime, message updates converge to the unique fixed point of the ENMP equations in finitely many iterations, yielding exact marginals; in the approximate regime, ENMP provides approximate marginals. For Gaussian factor graphs, we derive closed-form update rules enabling exact variance estimation in the exact regime, addressing the long-standing inaccurate variance estimates of loopy Gaussian BP. We evaluate ENMP on densely loopy Gaussian factor graphs from power-grid benchmarks and on a discrete Ising factor graph. Results show accuracy improves with neighborhood size, with exact marginals achieved on several systems in both settings. On larger Gaussian systems, ENMP outperforms regularized Gaussian BP (sGaBP-m) in both mean and variance estimation accuracy.

papers.title: Modelling the Nordic power system expansion with PyPSA-Eur: a comparison with the Nordic Grid Development Perspective 2025
papers.summary: We compare the Nordic Grid Development Perspective 2025 (NGDP) with a least-cost transition pathway for the Nordic power system obtained with PyPSA-Eur for the period 2025-2050 under a net-zero CO$_2$ constraint. The model co-optimises generation, storage, and transmission expansion with hourly system operation while constraining the Nordic generation mix to remain consistent with NGDP milestone ranges. Overall, the optimised capacity pathways reproduce the broad NGDP expansion of wind and solar power, with Denmark emerging as the main locus of offshore wind and solar deployment, Finland as a major site for onshore wind expansion, and Norway and Sweden relying more strongly on existing hydropower and nuclear capacity. The main discrepancy between the two pathways does not lie in the broad build-out of variable renewables, but in the timing and role of hydrogen. Whereas the NGDP treats hydrogen as an early and steadily increasing component of industrial demand and system development already from 2030, PyPSA-Eur delays substantial hydrogen deployment until 2045-2050, when it becomes cost-effective primarily as a flexibility and seasonal storage option in a strongly variable-renewable-energy-dominated system. This contrast suggests that early hydrogen build-out in the Nordics is not a robust outcome of cost optimisation alone, but depends strongly on assumptions regarding industrial demand growth, sector coupling, and anticipatory infrastructure planning. We therefore argue that hydrogen remains the principal strategic uncertainty in the Nordic transition, with the NGDP representing a more anticipatory planning perspective and PyPSA-Eur a more conservative least-cost timing of deployment.

papers.title: Towards Signal Processing In Networks: Multiplierless Block Transforms in Data Plane
papers.summary: In this paper, we propose a signal processing concept, signal processing in networks (SPIN), that executes signal processing tasks directly on programmable switches. Traditionally, signal processing tasks, such as denoising, decomposition, and dimensionality reduction, are performed on edge or cloud servers, i.e., raw streams are transmitted from sensors. This imposes a heavy processing load on edge/cloud servers and requires substantial bandwidth. SPIN addresses this problem by performing signal processing on the forwarding path. As an initial realization of SPIN, we implement a DCT-based block transform on a programmable switch. We redesign its computation using a lifting-based lattice structure, multiplierless approximation, and pipeline partitioning across stages in a programmable switch. We verify at the compiler level that the proposed implementation satisfies the strict hardware constraints of the Intel Tofino2--specifically regarding pipeline stages, packet header vector, and ternary content-addressable memory usage--and therefore enables line-rate processing. We further quantify the per-packet latency of the ingress match-action pipeline. The SPIN-oriented preprocessing adds 46 cycles (approximately 31 ns at 1.5 GHz). The total ingress match-action unit latency is approximately 87 ns, which remains consistent with the low-latency operation targeted by SPIN. Furthermore, we implement the proposed block transform on a BMv2 switch using P4 and evaluate it as preprocessing for in-network machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves classification performance over unfiltered baselines.

papers.title: Scalable Quantum Clustering of Renewable Profiles via a Hybrid Qubit-efficient Strategy
papers.summary: Large-scale renewable energy profile clustering is a computationally challenging NP-hard problem. Recent quantum computing techniques offer a potential remedy, yet their scalability is severely constrained by the limited qubit count of current quantum hardware. To address this issue, we first cast the problem into a QUBO form and then we propose a consensus-based variable reduction (CBVR) method to drastically cut qubit usage. More specifically, we tailor the one-hot constraint to eliminate assignment variables and leverage consensus analysis to convert stable clustering relations from initial anneals into equality constraints for further reduction. Experiments on real quantum hardware confirm that CBVR compresses oversized QUBO models into feasible sizes while retaining high clustering quality and efficiency.

papers.title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals
papers.summary: Secure transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains a major challenge in telecardiology. While traditional mathematical watermarking can embed patient metadata directly into ECG signals, it is highly fragile against temporal desynchronization such as circular phase shifts. In contrast, existing deep watermarking approaches for temporal signals, such as audio, typically rely on lossy quantization, which compromises the high-frequency micro-morphological details critical for clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we propose ECGWmark, a fully convolutional and quantization-free deep watermarking framework for medical time-series. ECGWmark operates in a continuous, full-resolution latent space and utilizes a localized frame-level mechanism to improve the robustness to severe desynchronization. Crucially, we introduce a differentiable Physiological Loss guided by a clinical classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Experiments on the benchmark MIT-BIH database show that ECGWmark maintains channel-bit extraction accuracy above 90% under the evaluated circular temporal shifts. Furthermore, under a rigorous inter-patient diagnostic evaluation, Class-V sensitivity changes from 71.97% to 76.50%, whereas Macro-F1 changes from 35.25% to 34.71% and Class-S sensitivity from 8.89% to 1.39%; these results indicate mixed class-level effects.

papers.title: Radiomics-Based Thyroid Nodule Classification with Label-Conditional Conformal Prediction
papers.summary: Thyroid nodule malignancy assessment relies on ultrasound imaging, yet current risk stratification systems suffer from substantial interobserver variability, contributing to a high rate of unnecessary biopsies. We propose a radiomics-based framework combining quantitative feature extraction via PyRadiomics with a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) classifier, selected among six candidates for its favorable trade-off between discriminative performance and interpretability. To complement point predictions with uncertainty estimates, Cross-Conformal Prediction with label-conditional guarantees is applied, flagging ambiguous cases for clinical review rather than forcing a binary decision. Experiments are conducted on TN5000, a publicly available ultrasound dataset of thyroid nodules. After Spearman correlation filtering, 36 features are retained and the GAM achieves an AUC of $0.89$, a sensitivity of $0.83$, and a specificity of $0.82$ on the validation set. At a significance level $\epsilon=0.09$, selected to ensure empirical coverage guarantees on both classes, 63\% of nodules on the test set receive a certain (i.e., single-label) prediction, with conditional precision of $0.94$ for certain malignant and conditional Negative Predictive Value (NPV) of $0.73$ for certain benign cases, while the remaining 37\% are referred to the clinician.

papers.title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas
papers.summary: We propose a coupling-aware tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) using reconfigurable parasitic antennas. Numerical results demonstrate that the transmit array introduces impedance mismatch that reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array. Moreover, the proposed tri-hybrid architecture significantly outperforms hybrid precoding by constructively exploiting the coupling effects, yielding substantial gains in spectral efficiency (SE) and sum non-linear harvested energy (NLHE) at a fraction of the hardware cost.

papers.title: Minimum-Energy Control for Stochastic Linear Systems
papers.summary: The open-loop minimum-energy control (MEC) problem asks for control inputs that minimize the control energy while ensuring the terminal state reaches a desired value. In this paper, we study the open-loop MEC problem for stochastic linear time-invariant systems. We consider a variety of stochastic constraints that enforce the terminal error to be \emph{small}, and show that Stochastic MEC (SMEC) problem can be formulated as a QCQP. We obtain the optimal solution for SMEC and show that it generalizes the well-known Deterministic MEC problem by introducing novel stochastic variants of controllability and Gramian matrices. Finally, we show that there exists a fundamental lower bound on the optimal control energy which cannot be overcome by increasing the time horizon of the problem.

papers.title: Blind and Asynchronous Initial Beam Acquisition and Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition in Standalone Mobile MIMO-OFDM Systems
papers.summary: Building upon our preliminary study, this paper proposes a standalone beam-management framework for mobile MIMO-OFDM systems that integrates Blind Initial Beam Acquisition (BIBA) with Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition (CARA). BIBA is a blind and asynchronous protocol that requires neither prior synchronization nor an out-of-band feedback channel, so the Base Station (BS) and User Equipment (UE) can independently identify the beam pair maximizing received signal strength. To handle subsequent link drops, the newly introduced CARA protocol exploits the clock synchronization established after BIBA to reduce the re-acquisition time by approximately 55% compared with BIBA. The operational reliability of both protocols is bounded by a probabilistic feasibility analysis under random UE mobility trajectories. Protocols are validated on a 28 GHz mmWave testbed under practical hardware constraints, including beam-switching and Time Division Duplex (TDD) latencies, and measured Software-Defined Radio (SDR) software processing delays. Finally, we formulate a unified Finite State Machine (FSM) model for both BIBA and CARA to ensure robust integration into practical wireless systems

papers.title: Suppressing Multiple GNSS Interferers with Local-Gradient Adaptive Notch Filtering
papers.summary: Adaptive notch filters (ANFs) based on the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm are an established technique for suppressing narrowband interference in GNSS receivers. The traditional solution for multiple interferers is simply cascading the NLMS-ANF into multiple stages but this solution degrades performance when multiple chirp jammers of similar power are present. We propose a low-complexity modification to the cascaded NLMS-ANF update rule to resolve this: a local gradient (LG) formulation: LG-ANF. The LG-ANF forms a locally bandlimited gradient signal by translating the input to baseband around the current frequency estimate, low-pass filtering it, and translating it back, thereby attenuating competing interferers before adaptation. The modification generalizes the traditional NLMS-ANF to handle the similar-power multiple interferer problem, using just one additional parameter. We characterize the gradient-averaging failure analytically and visually, demonstrate independent chirp tracking in the worst-case two-chirp scenarios, and evaluate statistical suppression performance by sweeping amplitude ratio against a standard NLMS-ANF, a frequency-locked-loop (FLL)-based ANF and a per-sample oracle upper bound. We further characterize the LG advantage over various ANF parameters and chirp conditions. Simulations show that the LG-ANF reduces to the standard NLMS-ANF outside the pathological multi-chirp regime, while recovering up to 4dB of in-band suppression around pathological amplitude ratios under per-condition optimization of the local bandwidth, and up to 13dB for selected edge-case parameter combinations. These optimized results represent an upper bound on the achievable LG gain. In a hardware experiment using a fixed alpha_lp=0.5, the LG-ANF extends position-lock survival by 24s relative to the standard ANF.

papers.title: Adaptive Incentive Design for Linear-Quadratic Dynamic Games: No-Regret Social Coordination
papers.summary: Incentives can align private interests with collective goals, but their design becomes intertwined with learning when agents' preferences are unknown. This paper develops an adaptive incentive-design framework for multi-agent linear-quadratic dynamic games, where a system planner can simultaneously learn agents' private preferences and steer their strategic behavior towards the social optimum. To this end, we first characterize the complete family of affine incentives that implement the social optimum as the unique open-loop Nash equilibrium while ensuring exact budget balance. When agents' preferences are unknown, we develop an online algorithm to estimate their preference parameters and establish strong consistency of the estimates under a weak trajectory-dependent excitation condition, without requiring persistent excitation or i.i.d. trajectories. We then integrate this estimator into an active-learning incentive mechanism that combines certainty-equivalent coordination with decaying random probing. We prove that the probing generates sufficient information through the agents' equilibrium responses and the system dynamics, ensuring consistent preference learning from the resulting closed-loop trajectories. We show that the induced trajectories converge almost surely to their socially optimal counterparts, while cumulative social-cost regret relative to the full-information oracle and cumulative net-budget imbalance grow sublinearly. Simulations of a transboundary pollution game demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Hierarchical Graph Neural Network for Probabilistic Power Flow with Grid Topology Contingencies
papers.summary: Data-driven surrogates reduce the nonlinear solves required for probabilistic power flow (PPF), but models tied to a fixed bus--branch graph often generalize poorly when outages change electrical coupling. This paper proposes a topology-decomposition-driven hierarchical bidirectional graph neural network (TDD--HBGNN) for PPF under unseen topologies. For each realized topology, the network is decomposed into fundamental topological units (FTUs), dynamically homogeneous voltage clusters (DHVCs), and a core backbone sub-grid (CBSG), with equivalent-admittance representations preserving electrical ports between units. A sensitivity-based linear prior captures the first-order voltage-magnitude and phase-angle response, while the HBGNN learns topology-dependent nonlinear residuals. Impedance- and uncertainty-aware bottom-up aggregation condenses local perturbations, while mode-modulated top-down broadcasting restores system context at buses. We evaluate our approach on the IEEE 118-bus and Polish 2746-bus systems under unseen N--1 and N--2 contingencies against six baseline methods. Compared with these methods, TDD--HBGNN achieves 2.47--4.20-fold lower all-bus phase-angle errors and lower phase-angle errors in every held-out event. Its voltage-magnitude advantage is concentrated near the outaged branches, where paired error ratios reach 1.75--2.58 on the IEEE system and 1.87--1.97 in Polish N--2 events. All system--contingency--baseline comparisons favor TDD--HBGNN in joint voltage--angle error. Moreover, shared hierarchical operators keep the model size at 0.658 million parameters across both grids and yield 0.161--1.793~ms forward latency per probabilistic case. These results demonstrate system-wide angular accuracy, outage-local voltage accuracy, and parameter-efficient scaling across unseen topologies.
